units.la: DISPUTATIO De PRIMATU PETRI APOSTOLI.
units.tr: DISPUTATION ON THE PRIMACY OF THE APOSTLE PETER.

units.la: 1. INTER Catholicos & Pontificios famosa agitatur Controversia; Utrum Pontifex Romanus sit Vicarius Christi, Caput Ecclesiæ Christianæ, omnium Christianorum Pater & Doctor, cui plenaria potestas ac jurisdictio infallibilis Universam Ecclesiam pascendi ac gubernandi; hæreticos præterea excommunicandi, tradita sit?
units.tr: 1. Between Catholics and Papists a famous controversy is being waged: Whether the Roman Pontiff is the Vicar of Christ, the Head of the Christian Church, the Father and Teacher of all Christians, to whom has been given full power and infallible jurisdiction to feed and govern the whole Church, and also to excommunicate heretics?

units.la: Affirmativam tueri conatur Papistarum pars illa, quæ Papam Conciliis simpliciter anteponit; contradicit illa, quæ eundem Conciliis subjicit.
units.tr: The affirmative is defended by that part of the Papists which places the Pope simply above the Councils; the other part, which makes him subject to the Councils, contradicts this.

units.la: Nos illos, falsò de unanimi consensu gloriantes, inter se committimus, ac Negativam tuemur.
units.tr: We leave those two parties, who falsely boast of a unanimous consent, to contend with each other, and we defend the negative.

units.la: 2. Ad tantæ controversiæ legitimam tractationem, sequentia, sine quibus omnis disputatio frustranea est, utrinque, tanquam communia principia, supponenda judicamus.
units.tr: 2. For a lawful treatment of so great a controversy, we judge that the following points, without which every disputation is futile, must be assumed on both sides as common principles.

units.la: α. Judicem supremum hujus & omnium de Religione controversiarum, nullum alium esse quàm Spiritum S. loquentem in Scriptura Prophetarum & Apostolorum: argumento locorum Jerem. 31. v. 39. 40. Ezech. II. v. 19. 20. & 36. v. 26. 27. Joh. 14. v. 26. & 15. v. 26. & 16. v. 13. 1. Cor. 12. v. 3. 9. 2. Petr. I. v. 20. 21.
units.tr: a. That the supreme judge of this and of all controversies about religion is none other than the Holy Spirit speaking in the Scripture of the Prophets and Apostles; proved from the passages Jer. 31:39, 40; Ezek. 11:19, 20; 36:26, 27; John 14:26; 15:26; 16:13; 1 Cor. 12:3, 9; 2 Pet. 1:20, 21.

units.la: β. S. Scripturam, ceu Spiritus Sancti vocem & sententiam, esse normam & regulam, secundum quam solam hæc, &c, aliæ controversiæ decidendæ, 2. Timoth. 3. v. 16. 17. Roman.6. v. 17. Galat.6. v.16. Phil.3.v.16. 2.Tim.1.v.13. Hinc Deuter.4. v.2. & 5. v.32. & 12. v.32. Gal.8. v.9. Apocal.22. v.18.19. adde Esaj.8.20.
units.tr: b. That the Holy Scripture, as the voice and sentiment of the Holy Spirit, is the norm and rule by which alone this and other controversies are to be decided: 2 Tim. 3:16, 17; Rom. 6:17; Gal. 6:16; Phil. 3:16; 2 Tim. 1:13. Hence Deut. 4:2; 5:32; 12:32; Gal. 1:8, 9; Rev. 22:18, 19; add Isa. 8:20.

units.la: γ. Judicem humanum, (quem Spiritus Sancti Ministrum, seu Ministerialem Judicem appellamus) omnem & solum audiendum dicimus, qui secundum mentem & sententiam Spiritus Sancti in S. Scriptura expressam pronunciat: omnem vero eum, qui ab ea recedit, quisquis ille sit, repudiandum nec audiendum. Esaj. 8. v.20. Jerem.23. v.16.17. Rom.12. v. 6. Matth.7. v.15.16.&c. 1.Joh.4.v.1. 1.Thefs.5. v.21. 2.Johan. v.10. Laudabile exemplu proponitur. Act.17.11.
units.tr: c. That we say the human judge (whom we call the minister, or ministerial judge, of the Holy Spirit) is to be heard in everything and only when he pronounces according to the mind and sentiment of the Holy Spirit expressed in Holy Scripture; but every man who departs from it, whoever he is, is to be rejected and not heard: Isa. 8:20; Jer. 23:16, 17; Rom. 12:6; Matt. 7:15, 16, etc.; 1 John 4:1; 1 Thess. 5:21; 2 John 10. A commendable example is set forth: Acts 17:11.

units.la: In his principiis, nisi Papistæ cum Catholicis convene-rint, oleum & opera perditur; imo cum negantibus hæc principia, præsertim in hac tanti momenti Controversia, non disputandum asserimus.
units.tr: Unless the Papists agree with the Catholics on these principles, oil and labour are wasted; indeed, we assert that no disputation should be held with those who deny these principles, especially in a controversy of such great importance.

units.la: ʒ. Itaque in limine disputationis, causæ suæ infirmitatem manifeste prodidit ille, qui non ita pridem liberè confessus est, in S. Scriptura nullum inveniri Catholicum argumentum, quo thesis hac probari possit: & iterum atq; iterum; ex Verbo Dei solo nihil probari posse, cum in Bibliis nulla Episcopi Romani fiat mentio: addit, neque auctoritate Judicis Ecclesiastici, absq; argumento Theologico thesin hanc confirmari posse. Et frustra ridet hoc nomine adversarios suos triumphan-tes;
units.tr: c. Therefore, at the threshold of the disputation, he who not long ago freely confessed that in Holy Scripture there is no Catholic argument by which this thesis can be proved; and again and again, nothing can be proved from the Word of God alone, since no mention of the Roman Bishop is made in the Bible*; he adds that this thesis cannot be confirmed without a theological argument even by the authority of an ecclesiastical judge, revealed the weakness of his cause plainly; and in vain does he mock his opponents on this account as if they were triumphing.

units.la: Etenim, (ut reliquam horum verborum censuram sicco pede præteream) quod de Argumento Theologico dicit; aut ejus consequentia fundamentum habet in Sacra Scriptura; aut non habet. Si nullum habet in Sacra Scriptura fundamentum, Theologicum argumentum esse negamus, simpliciter rejicimus, sicque Primatum Pontificis, jure divino destitutum, merito repudiamus. Si vero, (ut callide refervässe[?] id videtur) fundamentum in Sacra Scriptura habere præsumit, sibimet contradicit, quum ait, nullum inveniri in S. Scriptura Catholicum argumentum, aut, solo Dei verbo confirmari non posse. Nisi forte Verbum Dei esse neget id, quod legitimâ consequentiâ juxta mentem Spiritus S. inde elicitur; quo ipso tamen causam suam deteriorem redderet.
units.tr: For (to pass lightly over the rest of his judgement on these words) as to what he says about a theological argument: either its consequence has a foundation in Holy Scripture, or it has not. If it has no foundation in Holy Scripture, we deny that it is a theological argument, we reject it outright, and so we justly repudiate a Primacy of the Pontiff destitute of divine right. But if, as he seems to have cunningly hinted, he presumes it has a foundation in Holy Scripture, he contradicts himself, when he says that no Catholic argument is found in Holy Scripture, or that it cannot be confirmed by the Word of God alone. Unless perhaps he denies that to be the Word of God which is drawn from it by a legitimate consequence according to the mind of the Holy Spirit; yet by this very thing he would make his cause worse.

units.la: 4. Aut igitur expressè & evidenter in S. Scriptura de Pon-tifice Romano ejusque primatu agitur: aut implicitè. Illud liberè negat ille; neque ullus adversariorum id asserere audet. Ergò aut prorsus causâ cadant oportet, aut implicitè in S. Sancta contineri Primatum & Potestatem tantam Episcopi Romani fatendum est. Agitè igitur experiamur pondus Argumenti Theologici.
units.tr: 4. Therefore either the Roman Pontiff and his primacy are treated expressly and clearly in Holy Scripture, or implicitly. He flatly denies the former, and none of the opponents dares to assert it. Therefore either their cause must altogether fall, or it must be admitted that so great a primacy and power of the Roman Bishop is contained implicitly in the Holy Scripture. Let us then test the weight of the theological argument.

units.la: 5. Principale & ex N. T. unicum argumentum, hoc est, „ Quos dignitatis & potestatis titulos, Christus Petro Apostolo tribuit, eosdem quoque in Petro Christus tribuit legitimo ejus Successori Episcopo Rom. „ Atqui Christus Petro Apostolo ejusmodi titulos tribuit, quòd sit Vicarius ipsius, Caput Ecclesiæ, &c. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: 5. The principal and only argument from the New Testament is this: "The titles of dignity and power which Christ gave to the Apostle Peter, the same Christ also gave in Peter to his lawful successor, the Roman Bishop." "But Christ gave to the Apostle Peter titles of this kind, that he is his Vicar, the Head of the Church, etc." Therefore, etc.

units.la: 6. Ad hoc argumentum respondemus
units.tr: 6. To this argument we reply:

units.la: a. Ex hypothesi adversarii. V. M. hoc argumentum esse, aut Catholicum, Judicis Ecclesiastici, ideoque coactivum; aut Theologicum seu oratorium, morale & persuasivum.
units.tr: a. On the hypothesis of the opponent, this argument must be either a Catholic argument of an ecclesiastical judge, and therefore compulsory; or a theological or oratorical argument, moral and persuasive.

units.la: At non prius; ratio, quia
units.tr: But not the former; the reason being that

units.la: I.[?] Judex ille Ecclesiasticus, id est, Pontifex Romanus, in hac causa nec Testis, nec Judex esse potest
units.tr: 1. That ecclesiastical judge, that is, the Roman Pontiff, can be neither witness nor judge in this cause.

units.la: 2. ab omni errore immunis esset esseque deberet; si enim errare posset, Catholicum ac coactivum infallibilis Judicis argumentum non esset. Atqui erroneum, non autem Catholicum esse, jam jam manifestum fiet.
units.tr: 2. He would be, and ought to be, free from every error; for if he could err, it would not be a Catholic and compulsory argument of an infallible judge. But that it is erroneous and not Catholic will soon become plain.

units.la: Nec posterius: si enim hoc argumentū Theologicum est, tùm aut Biblicum est, aut non est:
units.tr: Nor the latter: for if this is a theological argument, then either it is biblical or it is not.

units.la: Si non est Biblicum, tùm, positis superioribus principiis, illud jure merito ceu humani cerebri figmentum rejicimus.
units.tr: If it is not biblical, then, given the principles stated above, we justly reject it as a figment of the human brain.

units.la: Si Biblicum est, tùm, ex hypothesi adversarii, hæreticorum est, ideoque apud ipsos Pontificios nullius ponderis.
units.tr: If it is biblical, then, on the hypothesis of the opponent, it belongs to the heretics, and therefore has no weight even with the Papists themselves.

units.la: Hæc ad personam.
units.tr: So much for the person.

units.la: Ad rem: dicimus fundamentum hoc ad tantam molem sustinendam nimis infirmum, & arenosum esse. Etenim
units.tr: As to the matter: we say this foundation is too weak and sandy to bear so great a mass. For

units.la: Major nec demonstrativa, nec dialectica; sed apatetica, sed Sophistica est: Supponit enim
units.tr: The major premise is neither demonstrative nor dialectical, but apatetic, indeed sophistical. For it presupposes

units.la: Petrum fuisse Episcopum Romanum.
units.tr: that Peter was the Roman Bishop;

units.la: Ejusdem Petri legitimum Successorem esse Episcopum Romanum, idq; 1. in Sede. 2. in Officio. 3. in Doctrina. 4. idque continua successione in omnibus ad hodiernum usque diem. 5. in omni prærogativa, quam Episcopi Rom. sibi arrogant, usurpant & exercent.
units.tr: that the lawful successor of this same Peter is the Roman Bishop, and that in 1. the See, 2. the office, 3. the doctrine, 4. and this by continuous succession down to the present day, 5. in every prerogative which the Roman Bishops claim for themselves, usurp and exercise.

units.la: Quæ omnia nec Catholico, nec Theologico argumento, neque ulla legitima consequentiâ, non Concilium Florentinum, nec ullum aliud; nullus vel venerandâ canitie suspiciendus, vel pietate venerabilis, vel doctrinâ celebris, absque circulo probabit unquam.
units.tr: All of which no one, however worthy of respect for venerable grey hairs, or venerable for piety, or famous for learning, will ever prove, without circular reasoning, either by a Catholic and theological argument, or by any legitimate consequence, nor the Council of Florence, nor any other.

units.la: Sed missâ Majore; cùm τὸ πρῶτον ψεῦδος [?] lateat in Minore, pernegamus illam. Itaque quæstio prima & principalis hæc est,
units.tr: But, setting aside the major premise, since the first falsehood [τὸ πρῶτον ψεῦδος] lies hidden in the minor, we flatly deny it. Therefore the first and principal question is this:

units.la: „ An Christus Petrum constituerit Vicarium suum, „ Caput Ecclesiæ Universale, &c?
units.tr: "Whether Christ appointed Peter as his Vicar, the Universal Head of the Church," etc.?

units.la: Hanc si probaverint adver-sarii, manus dabimus; sin verò, totum ædificium, quod huic fundamento super-struunt, mole suâ ruiturum confidenter asserimus.
units.tr: If the opponents prove this, we shall yield; but if not, we confidently assert that the whole edifice which they build upon this foundation will fall by its own weight.

units.la: 7. Ut autem ordine progrediamur, videbimus
units.tr: 7. But that we may proceed in order, we shall see

units.la: α. Præcipua Pontificiorum argumenta:
units.tr: a. the principal arguments of the Papists;

units.la: β. Catholicorum opponemus rationes.
units.tr: b. the reasons which we Catholics oppose to them.

units.la: 8. Primum & principale argumentum Pontificiorum in forma ita habet:
units.tr: 8. The first and principal argument of the Papists runs in this form:

units.la: Qui est Petra, supra quam Christus ædificavit Ecclesiam suam, illum Christus constituit suum Vicarium, Caput Ecclesiæ, &c. Atqui Petrus est Petra, &c.
units.tr: He who is the Rock upon which Christ built his Church, Christ appointed as his Vicar, Head of the Church, etc. But Peter is the Rock, etc.

units.la: Respondemus:
units.tr: We reply:

units.la: {ℵ}[?] Materialiter; medium terminum distinguendo: Vocabulum enim Petra sumitur
units.tr: Materially; by distinguishing the middle term. For the word Rock is taken

units.la: Proprie, pro rupe, saxo, seu magnæ molis lapide; & iterum vel
units.tr: properly, for a crag, a stone, or a stone of great mass; and again either

units.la: Absolutè, pro rupe,&c. in se & qualitatibus, id est, robore, firmitate, & immobilitate, considerata.
units.tr: absolutely, considered in itself and in its qualities, that is, its strength, firmness and immobility.

units.la: Relatè vel
units.tr: Relatively, or

units.la: ut est terminus, regionem à regione, agrum ab agro discriminans.
units.tr: as it is a boundary, separating one region from another, one field from another.

units.la: ut est fundamentum alicujus ædificii. Matth. 7. v.24.&c.
units.tr: as it is the foundation of some building: Matt. 7:24, etc.

units.la: Improprie, & hoc diversimodè, vel
units.tr: Improperly, and this in various ways, or

units.la: Metaphoricè, quum dicitur Petra id, quod cum Petra proprie dictâ aliquam similitudinem habet, tùm respectu
units.tr: metaphorically, when that is called a Rock which has some likeness to a rock properly so called, then with respect

units.la: Qualitatis, id est, roboris, firmitatis, constantiæ & immobilitatis; & hæc Firmitas est vel
units.tr: to quality, that is, strength, firmness, constancy and immobility; and this firmness is either

units.la: Essentialis & propria; ita præter Deum nulla creatura Petra dici potest. Pf.18. v.3. Christus ergò, quia Deus, verè Petra dici potest.
units.tr: essential and proper, and so no creature apart from God can be called a Rock: Ps. 18:3. Therefore Christ, because he is God, can truly be called a Rock.

units.la: Accidentalis & communicata; & hâc significatione Petra, id est, instar Petræ dici potest Ecclesia Christi tota, & in ea non solùm Petrus, sed quivis firmâ fide præditus: Ita homo constans, quadratus instar lapidis appellatur.
units.tr: accidental and communicated; and in this sense the whole Church of Christ, and in it not only Peter but anyone endowed with a firm faith, can be called a rock, that is, like a rock; so a steadfast man is called squared like a stone.

units.la: Relationis tùm,
units.tr: Relational sense, then:

units.la: Quatenus illâ, nempe Petrâ, Ecclesia Christi à mundo, & singuli fideles ab infidelibus discernuntur: ita Fides in Christum, Confessio Christi, atq; adeò Christus, Petra dici potest: huic enim qui innititur, distinguitur eo ipso ab omni eo, qui extra Christum est: ita Petrus, & quivis fidelis, qui discernitur ab extraneis, non est Petra; sed id ipsum, Quo discernitur, Petra nuncupari potest.
units.tr: Since by it, namely the rock, the Church of Christ is distinguished from the world and individual believers from unbelievers, faith in Christ, the confession of Christ, and indeed Christ himself, can be called the rock. For whoever rests on this is thereby distinguished from everyone who is outside Christ. So Peter, or any believer who is distinguished from outsiders, is not the rock; but that by which he is distinguished can be called the rock.

units.la: Quatenus indigitatur fundamentum Ecclesiæ, cui superædificata, firmiter innititur, & adversus portas inferorum immota subsistit. Hæc significatio Principalis est, & indigitatur non simpliciter Petra; sed Petra Ecclesiæ, & quidem totius Ecclesiæ, tùm triumphantis, tùm militantis, tùm ejus quæ fuit in Vet. Testamento, tùm illius quæ est in Nov. Testamento; non enim aliud illius, aliud hujus Ecclesiæ fundamentum fuit unquam. Docet hoc relatio, quæ est inter duo correlata, quæ sunt Petra ceu fundamentum Spirituale, & Ecclesia ceu ædificium Spirituale: 1. Nunquam fingi posse unum absque altero; natura enim simul sunt Relata; ideoque nunquam Ecclesia sine fundamento, nec hoc sine illa fuit. 2. Præterea hæc eadem Relata ita distincta[?] esse, ut nunquam unum Relatorum sit alterum; itaque nunquam Petra est Ecclesia, aut Ecclesia Petra; quia Petra, Ecclesiæ Petra; & fundamentum, ædificii fundamentum est: Unde porrò manifestum; siquidem tota Ecclesia, Petra & fundamentum Ecclesiæ, adeoque sui ipsius dici nequeat, minùs individuum Ecclesiæ membrum, ideò Petrum, Ecclesiæ Petram, & sic sui ipsius, dici non posse.
units.tr: The sense in which the foundation of the Church is indicated, on which the Church is built and rests firmly, and which stands unmoved against the gates of hell. This is the principal sense, and the rock is indicated not simply as a rock but as the rock of the Church, and indeed of the whole Church, both triumphant and militant, both that which existed in the Old Testament and that which exists in the New Testament. For there never was one foundation for that Church and another for this one. The relation between two correlatives teaches this, namely the rock as the spiritual foundation and the Church as the spiritual building: (1) one can never be conceived without the other, for they are correlatives by nature and exist together; therefore the Church never existed without a foundation, nor the foundation without the Church. (2) Moreover, these same correlatives are so distinct that one of them is never the other; so the rock is never the Church, nor the Church the rock, because a rock is the rock of the Church, and a foundation is the foundation of a building. From this it is further clear that, since the whole Church is the rock and foundation of the Church, it cannot be called itself, and still less an individual member of the Church. Therefore Peter, who is a rock of the Church, cannot be called the rock of himself.

units.la: Itaq; in hac significatione Petra Ecclesiæ dicitur 1. quæ non est Ecclesia, nec pars ulla Ecclesiæ. 2. quæ tamen cum Ecclesia ejusque membris, habeat aliquam convenientiam & similitudinem; ut imus angularis lapis cum lapidibus, qui ei superædificantur. 3. ut Ecclesiâ major, fortior, suâque naturâ immobilis sit. 4. Ut ad ædificium in se recipiendum, sustinendum corroborandum & confervandum ordinata & idonea sit. nei[?] fit. Quibus positis palàm est, præter Christum Petram Ecclesiæ nullam esse.
units.tr: Thus in this sense something is called the rock of the Church: (1) which is not the Church, nor any part of the Church; (2) which nevertheless has some agreement and likeness with the Church and its members, as the corner stone has with the stones built upon it; (3) which is greater and stronger than the Church and is immovable by its nature; (4) which is fitted and suited to receive, sustain, strengthen and preserve the building in itself. With these points established, it is plain that apart from Christ there is no rock of the Church.

units.la: Metonymicè. nempe per metonymiam adjuncti occupati pro subjecto vel objecto occupante: quo sensu Petra Ecclesiæ dici potest,
units.tr: Metonymically, namely by metonymy of the adjunct put for the subject or object that is occupied with it. In this sense Peter can be called the rock of the Church,

units.la: α. Fides, tùm
units.tr: (a) faith, both

units.la: Qua creditur; id est, doctrina Evangelii de Petra Ecclesiæ, nempe Christo; hoc sensu, Ephes. 2. verf. 20. dicuntur Fideles superstructi super fundamentum Prophetarum & Apostolorum, id est, super doctrinam eorum, cui etiam ipsi Prophetæ & Apostoli innixi: & 1. Corinth.3.10. dicit Paulus, se primum Ecclesiam Corinthiacam fundamentum posuisse, id est, doctrinam Evangelii, adeoque Christum, primum illis annunciasse. Hinc ut Petra Ecclesiæ; ita doctrina Verbi Dei æterna dicitur: Matth. 24. v.35. 1. Petr. 1. ult.
units.tr: by which it is believed; that is, the doctrine of the Gospel concerning the rock of the Church, namely Christ. In this sense, Ephesians 2:20 says that believers are built upon the foundation of the prophets and apostles, that is, upon their doctrine, on which the prophets and apostles themselves also rested. And in 1 Corinthians 3:10 Paul says that he had laid the foundation of the Corinthian Church first, that is, that he had first announced to them the doctrine of the Gospel and so Christ. Hence, just as Peter is the rock of the Church, so the doctrine of the Word of God is called eternal: Matthew 24:35; 1 Peter 1 at the end.

units.la: Qua creditur; non qua actus aut opus est; est enim actus transiens, quandoque infirmus, nunquam perfectus: sed qua apprehendit Petram Ecclesiæ; hinc ut justitia fidei, ita Petra fidei; seu ut Fides Victoria nostra, ita Fides Petra nostra dici potest. Rom. 4. v.11.13. 1. Joh.5. v.4.5. quo sensu Paulus Colos. 2. v. 6. 7. ait: Sicut accepistis Christum Jesum Dominum, ita in eo incedite, radicati & superstructi in eo, ac confirmati fide.
units.tr: By which it is believed; not as an act or work. For faith is a transitive act, sometimes weak and never perfect; rather it is the faith by which one apprehends the rock of the Church. Hence, as the righteousness of faith is the faith-righteousness, so the rock of faith may be called the rock of faith; or as faith is our victory, so faith may be called our rock. Romans 4:11, 13; 1 John 5:4, 5. In this sense Paul says in Colossians 2:6, 7: As you have received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in him, rooted and built up in him, and established in the faith.

units.la: β. Confessio fidei, qua Petrus aut quivis fidelis confitetur, Petram, id est, Jesum esse Christum, Filium Dei viventis: Huc facit quod habetur Rom.10. v.10. & hoc sensu plerique Patres Petram interpretantur.
units.tr: (b) The confession of faith, by which Peter or any believer confesses the rock, that is, that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God. To this belongs what is found in Romans 10:10, and in this sense most of the Fathers interpret the rock.

units.la: γ. Deniq; Petra dici potest, Qui ministerio suo ædificat Ecclesiam, eamque sustinet, fideliter Christum Petram annunciando, ad fidem in Christum & perseverantiâ in fide exhortando & confirmando: quo sensu Apostoli magnâ gaudent prærogativa: Etenim His primis non caro & sanguis; sed Pater coelestis Christum revelavit.
units.tr: (c) Finally, the rock can be called one who by his ministry builds the Church, and sustains it, faithfully announcing Christ as the rock, exhorting and confirming people to faith in Christ and perseverance in the faith. In this sense the apostles enjoy a great prerogative, for not flesh and blood, but the heavenly Father revealed Christ to these first ones.

units.la: Hi primi Christum annunciando, Ecclesiam N. Testamenti fundarunt & aedificarunt.
units.tr: These first ones, by announcing Christ, founded and built the Church of the New Testament.

units.la: Hi primi non particularis alicujus, sed universalis Ecclesiae fundamenta jecerunt.
units.tr: These first ones laid the foundations not of some particular church, but of the universal Church.

units.la: Hi primi & soli infallibilitatis in doctrina privilegium habuerunt.
units.tr: These first ones alone had the privilege of infallibility in doctrine.

units.la: Amplius dico: Inter hos omnes Petrus primus Jesum esse Christum, Filium Dei viventis, ore suo confessus est: primus Pentecostes die publice Christum, imum angularem lapidem praedicando, N. Testamenti Ecclesiae fundamenta jecit; & supra Christum aedificare coepit.
units.tr: Furthermore I say: among all these, Peter first confessed with his mouth that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God. On the day of Pentecost he was the first to preach Christ publicly, the chief corner stone, and so laid the foundations of the Church of the New Testament and began to build upon Christ.

units.la: Addo, singularibus donis, ardenti inprimis Zelo, a Spiritu Sancto dotatus fuit.
units.tr: I add that he was endowed by the Holy Spirit with singular gifts, above all with a burning zeal.

units.la: Ast vero si primus, non solus tamen; etsi multum aedificarit, non tamen omne;
units.tr: But, if he was first, he was nevertheless not alone; and although he built much, he did not build everything.

units.la: Itaque Petrus Petra fit, Columna fit; non solus tamen. Gal.2.v.9. non solus, nec ordine primus Columna dicitur; sed a Paulo Columna dicuntur, Jacobus, Cephas, & Johannes. Paulus appellatur Christi σκεῦος[?] ἐκλογῆς A&:9.v.15. non inferior summis Apostolis. 2.Cor.11.5. & cap.12.11. amplius quam caeteri Apostoli omnes laboravit. 1.Cor.15.10.
units.tr: So Peter becomes a rock and becomes a pillar, but not alone. Galatians 2:9: he is not called the only pillar, nor the first in order; rather James, Cephas and John are called pillars. Paul is called a chosen vessel [σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς], Acts 9:15, and is not inferior to the chief apostles. 2 Corinthians 11:5 and chapter 12:11: he labored more abundantly than all the other apostles. 1 Corinthians 15:10.

units.la: Petrus Petra, Columna Ecclesiae fuerit, tempore, ordine, primus etiam dotibus (nisi forte palmam ei dubiam faciat Paulus) Petra tamen titulum specie diversum non habet, sed communem, non modo cum Apostolis, sed etiam cum Prophetis, Pastoribus & Doctoribus Ecclesiae, quod manifeste docet Christus Matth. 28.19.20. Et Paulus, Ephef.4.11.12. Pari ratione Ministri honoris ergo Patres spirituales dicuntur, non quod virtute sibi insita regenerent: sed quod ministri sint virtutis regeneratis, id est, Spiritus Christi. Confer. 1.Corinth.4.v.15. Galat.4.19. cum 1.Corinth.3. v.6.7.8.9. His ita præmissis, Formaliter respondemus
units.tr: Even if Peter was the rock and pillar of the Church in time, in rank, and even first in gifts (unless perhaps Paul makes the palm doubtful for him), rock is still not a title of a different kind for him, but a common one, shared not only with the apostles but also with the prophets, the ministers and teachers of the Church, as Christ clearly teaches in Matthew 28:19, 20, and Paul in Ephesians 4:11, 12. By the same reasoning, ministers are called spiritual fathers out of honour, not because they regenerate by any power inherent in themselves, but because they are ministers of the power of those regenerated, that is, of the Spirit of Christ. Compare 1 Corinthians 4:15 and Galatians 4:19 with 1 Corinthians 3:6, 7, 8, 9. With these points premised, we answer formally:

units.la: 1. Si major intelligatur vel de omni eo, quod Petra est aut esse dicitur omni sensu expósito supra, tum est salsissima; ratio; sic enim doctrina Christiana, fides, fidei confessio, Christi vicarius, caput Ecclesiæ, &c. esset, quod ne Pontificii quidem afferent.
units.tr: 1. If the major premise is understood of everything that is a rock, or is said to be one, in every sense set out above, then the reasoning is utterly false. For in that case Christian doctrine, faith, the confession of faith, the vicar of Christ, the head of the Church, and so on, would be the rock, which not even the Papists would assert.

units.la: de omni eo, qui est Petra; tum sequeretur
units.tr: If it is understood of everything that is the rock, then it would follow

units.la: α. Christum esse sui ipsius Vicarium,
units.tr: (a) that Christ is his own vicar;

units.la: β. non tantum Petrum, sed & cæteros Apostolos, ministros Evangelii singulos, quemvis Fidelem, imo totam Ecclesiam, esse vicarium Christi, caput Ecclesiæ, &c. quod alienum esse à vero, nemo non videt.
units.tr: (b) that not only Peter but also the other apostles, each minister of the Gospel, every believer, and indeed the whole Church, would be the vicar of Christ and the head of the Church, and so on. That this is foreign to the truth no one fails to see.

units.la: de omni eo, qui (præter Christum, Petram principaliter sic dictam) κατ' ἐξοχὴν, & prærogativâ singulari supra omnes mortales dicitur Petra Ecclesiæ, supra quam Christus Ecclesiam suam ædificaturus sit; tum major forte aliquo tolerabili sensu admitti posset: Sed de Vicariatu, præeminentiâ, potestate ac jurisdictione, quam Pontificii Papæ tribuunt, quamque sequiores Episcopi seu Pontifices Romani sibi arrogant & exercent, id est, de absoluta, impiâ & crudeli seu Tyrannica, majorem negamus: ratio; talem enim nec Christus habet, nec proin alii, minus suo vicario talem in Ecclesiam, corpus suum tradere voluit, aut potuit.
units.tr: If it is understood of that one who (apart from Christ, the rock in the principal and so-called sense) is called the rock of the Church par excellence [κατ' ἐξοχήν], and by singular prerogative above all mortals, the rock upon which Christ was to build his Church, then the major premise might perhaps be admitted in some tolerable sense. But concerning the vicariate, pre-eminence, power and jurisdiction which the Papists attribute to the Pope, and which the more recent bishops or Roman pontiffs claim for themselves and exercise, that is, concerning an absolute, impious and cruel or tyrannical power, we deny the major premise. The reason is that Christ has no such power, and therefore neither do others; nor did he wish or was able to hand over such power over the Church, his body, to his vicar.

units.la: 2. Minor vero salsissima est: Loquitur enim ea de Persona Petri & quidem sola, seclusò Christo, & exclusis reliquis Apostolis omnibus; ratio;
units.tr: 2. The minor premise, however, is utterly false. For it speaks of the person of Peter alone, apart from Christ and with all the other apostles excluded. The reason is:

units.la: α. quia, persona Petri, neque est doctrina, neque fides, neque confessio Petri, ideoque nec Petra esse aut dici potest.
units.tr: (a) because the person of Peter is neither the doctrine, nor the faith, nor the confession of Peter, and therefore he cannot be or be called the rock.

units.la: β. quia si metonymia resolvatur, sicque adjunctum occupatum in suum Objectum circa quod occupatur, tum dostrina Evangelii, fides & confessio ponuntur pro Christo, & ab hoc denominantur Petra: neque enim quaevis doctrina, neque quaevis fides aut confessio, Petra Ecclesiae dici potest: sed solùm doctrina de Christo, fides in Christum & confessio Christi; ita verò Persona Petri nullâ ratione resolvi potest, id est, Petrus pro Christo supponi nequit.
units.tr: (b) because if the metonymy is resolved, and so the adjunct occupied with its object with which it is concerned, then the doctrine of the Gospel, faith and confession are put for Christ, and are named the rock from him. For not every doctrine, nor every faith or confession, can be called the rock of the Church, but only the doctrine concerning Christ, faith in Christ, and the confession of Christ. But the person of Peter cannot be resolved in any way of this kind, that is, Peter cannot be substituted for Christ.

units.la: γ. quia si maximè Petrus Petra dici potest, sive quòd circa Ecclesiam supra Christum, Petram, aedificandam occupatus fuerit.
units.tr: γ. Because, if Peter can be called a rock at all, he can be so called chiefly because he was engaged in building the Church upon Christ, the Rock.

units.la: quòd firmus & immobilis per fidem Christo adhaeserit; tùm.
units.tr: Because he adhered to Christ by faith, firm and immovable; then:

units.la: 1. Non ratione personae suae; sed vel ratione officii sui, & quidem tantùm quatenus supra Christum aedificabat: vel ratione qualitatis, non propriae, sed communicatae à Christo & in Christo, Petra dici potuit.
units.tr: 1. He was not a rock by reason of his person, but either by reason of his office, and indeed only in so far as he was building upon Christ, or by reason of a quality not his own but communicated by Christ and in Christ.

units.la: 2. Non solus Petra est; sed & omnes Apostoli & horum in aedificanda Ecclesia successores: omnes item fide in Christo superstructi & radicati, qui in Petra illa ceu Petrae subsistunt immotae.
units.tr: 2. Peter is not the only rock. All the apostles are, and their successors in building the Church. Likewise all who are built up and rooted in faith in Christ, who stand in that rock as in a rock, unmoved.

units.la: 3. Minorem negatam probare conantur adversarii hoc argumento:
units.tr: 3. The opponents try to prove the denied minor by this argument:

units.la: Cui Christus dicit, Tu es Petrus, ille est Petra illa, supra quam, &c.
units.tr: To whom Christ says, "You are Peter," he is that rock upon which, etc.

units.la: At Simoni filio Jonae Christus dicit, Tu es Petrus. Ergò, &c.
units.tr: But Christ says to Simon son of Jonah, "You are Peter." Therefore, etc.

units.la: Resp. majorem negari:
units.tr: Reply: the major is denied.

units.la: Probant eam sic:
units.tr: They prove it thus:

units.la: Cui Christus dicit, Tu es Petra, ille est Petra illa, supra quam, &c.
units.tr: To whom Christ says, "You are a rock," he is that rock upon which, etc.

units.la: At cui dicit Christus, Tu es Petrus, ei dicit, Tu es Petra. Ergò
units.tr: But to whom Christ says, "You are Peter," to him he says, "You are a rock." Therefore

units.la: Rationem minoris adducunt hanc, quia in Syriacâ linguâ, in qua Christus loquutus est, utroq; loco eadem vox Cephas est, qua vox Petram significat.
units.tr: They give this reason for the minor: because in the Syriac language, in which Christ spoke, the same word, Cephas, stands in both places, and that word means a rock.

units.la: Respondemus
units.tr: We reply

units.la: 1. Ad majorem, eam negando: quia alia & diversa hujus vocabuli Cephas, significatio est in subjecto; alia in praedicato.
units.tr: 1. To the major, we deny it: because the meaning of this word Cephas is one thing as subject and another as predicate.

units.la: 2. Minor proin vera est in sensu Christi, falsa in sensu Pontificio.
units.tr: 2. The minor is therefore true in Christ's sense and false in the Papist sense.

units.la: 3. Hujus itaque probatio ab identitate literarum Syriaci vocabuli ad identitatem significationis frustranea est. Hic vero probe notandum.
units.tr: 3. So their proof, from the identity of the letters of the Syriac word to the identity of its meaning, is worthless. But here we must note well:

units.la: α. Pontificios, provocando ad Syriacam inguam (in qua Christum loquutum fuisse non diffitemur) tum infirmitate causae suae prodere, tum Authentiam vulgatae versionis, non absq; anathemate, in dubium vocare, ejusq; interpretationem subaccusare.
units.tr: α. By appealing to the Syriac language (in which we do not deny that Christ spoke), the Papists both betray the weakness of their cause and, not without anathema, call into doubt the authority of the Vulgate version and find fault with its interpretation.

units.la: β. Nos contra sequimur editionem Graecam, citra controversiam, authenticam; quam nō caro & sanguis, sed Pater coelestis Evangelistae revelavit, quamque Petrus cum reliquis Apostolis recepit, denique universa Ecclesia in hunc usq; diem retinuit, & porro retinebit. Ea vero Syriaca verba ita interpretatur, ut evidenter distinguat inter prius & posterius Cephas, sicq; hanc ipsam controversiam, quam Omniscius praeviderat, dirimat, ut ex sequentibus patescet.
units.tr: β. We, on the other hand, follow the Greek edition, which is beyond controversy authentic: the one which flesh and blood did not reveal to the Evangelist, but the heavenly Father did; which Peter received along with the other apostles; and which the whole Church has retained to this day and will go on retaining. That edition translates the Syriac words in such a way as clearly to distinguish between the first and the second Cephas, and so settles this very controversy, which the All-knowing had foreseen, as will be clear from what follows.

units.la: 9. Instant enim: Quod pronomine relativo τωύτῃ indigitatur, illud indigitatur nomine Petrae. At proxime antecedens scilic. Petrus indigitatur in nomine τωύτῃ. Ergo
units.tr: 9. For they press further: What is pointed out by the relative pronoun [ταύτῃ, "this"] is pointed out by the name Petra. But the immediately preceding word, namely Peter, is pointed out by the name [ταύτῃ]. Therefore

units.la: Resp. 1. Ad medium terminum: an pronomen τωύτῃ sit relativum, non est indubium: Christum seipsum indigitare voluisse, orthodoxorum est sententia, sive igitur digito aut manu pectori admota expresse se indigitaverit; sive absq; signo hanc ipsius suam [illegible, ~8 letters] esse significaverit, demonstrativum pronomen erit. Sicque major non admittitur.
units.tr: Reply 1. As to the middle term: it is not in doubt whether the pronoun [ταύτῃ] is relative. It is the opinion of the orthodox that Christ wished to point out himself. So whether he expressly indicated himself with a finger or with a hand laid on his breast, or without any sign signified that this was his own [illegible], it will be a demonstrative pronoun. And so the major is not admitted.

units.la: 2. Esto relativum: tum negamus minorem; idque ob sequentes rationes.
units.tr: 2. Granting that it is relative, we deny the minor, for the following reasons.

units.la: α. Pronomen relativum semper referri ad proximum antecedens negamus.
units.tr: α. We deny that a relative pronoun always refers to the immediately preceding antecedent.

units.la: β. Si ad proximè antecedens referri deberet, Christus in eodem genere perrexisset, dicendo: σὺ εἶ ὁ Πέ-τρος, καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ τῷ Πέτρῳ [?], &c. quid enim prohibuisset? 2. maximè si tantam praerogativam, non tantum super omnes reliquos Apostolos, sed etiam super universam Ecclesiam Petro tribuere voluisset. At vero ita ἐμφατικώτερον ait; σὺ εἶ Πέ-τρος, καὶ ἐπὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πέτρᾳ [?] &c. ita habet Graeca authentica; ita vulgata versio; imo omnes aliae, verba Christi ita reddiderunt, & inter Petrum & Petram distinguentes, hunc sensum Christi esse docent, quasi dixisset; Vere dixisti, me esse Christum, id est, Messiam & Unctum illum à Domino, Ecclesiae Re-demptorem, non unum ex Prophetis, seu nudum tantum hominem, sed Filium Dei Viventis adeo, verum quoque Deum, fundamentum & Petram Ecclesiae, & quia hoc non caro & sanguis, sed Pater meus cœlestis revelavit, ideo dico Tibi, Tu es Petrus, vivus lapis, supra me ædificatus fide; scito igitur me ἐπὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πέτρᾳ supra hanc ipsam Petram, quam confessus es, cui fide innixus es, ædificaturum Universam Ecclesiam meam, adeo ut quisquis tecum fide confessus fuerit, me esse Christum Filium Dei Viventis, vivus in me lapis & de Ecclesia mea fit futurus.
units.tr: β. If it had to refer to the immediately preceding word, Christ would have continued in the same pattern, saying: "You are the Peter [σὺ εἶ ὁ Πέτρος], and upon this Peter [καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ τῷ Πέτρῳ], etc." For what would have prevented him? Especially if he had wished to grant Peter such a pre-eminence, not only above all the other apostles but even above the whole Church. But in fact he says more emphatically: "You are Peter [σὺ εἶ Πέτρος], and upon this rock [καὶ ἐπὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πέτρᾳ], etc." So the authentic Greek has it, and so the Vulgate version has it. Indeed all the others have rendered Christ's words in this way, distinguishing between Peter and Rock, and teach that this is the sense of Christ, as if he had said: "You have truly said that I am Christ, that is, the Messiah and the Anointed of the Lord, the Redeemer of the Church, not one of the prophets or a mere man, but the Son of the living God, and indeed also true God, the foundation and rock of the Church. And because this was revealed not by flesh and blood but by my heavenly Father, therefore I say to you, You are Peter, a living stone built upon me by faith. Know therefore that I will build my whole Church [ἐπὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πέτρᾳ] upon this very rock which you have confessed, on which you lean by faith; so that whoever shall confess with you that I am Christ, the Son of the living God, will become a living stone in me and will be of my Church."

units.la: 10. Excipiunt tamen; Aliud docere novi nominis impositionem, Joh. 1. 43. promissam; ubi Christus ad Simonem; Tu vocaberis Cephas, ὁ ἑρμηνεύεται Πέτρος, quod Beza vertit, Quod declaratur Petra; unde sic argumentantur. Nomen Petri novum aut frustra impositum est, aut significat Petram illam, supra quam Christus ædificaturus est Ecclesiam. Illud nemo dicit. Itaque hoc necessario sequitur.
units.tr: 10. They object, however, that the imposition of a new name, promised in John 1:43 (Joh. 1. 43.), teaches something else. There Christ says to Simon: "You shall be called Cephas," [ὁ ἑρμηνεύεται Πέτρος], which Beza translates, "which is declared Rock." Whence they argue thus: "The new name Peter was either given in vain, or it signifies that rock upon which Christ is going to build his Church. No one says the former. Therefore the latter necessarily follows."

units.la: Resp. 1. Absit ut dicamus, Christum frustra & absque causa Simoni mutâsse nomen, & nominâsse Petrum; Sed ideo mutasse, ut innueret Petrum esse Petram, supra quam ædificaturus sit Ecclesiam suam, non sequitur: neq;'ex eo, quod promisit Christus Joh. 1.45. Simonem appellandum Petrum, neque ex interpretatione Petræ probatur. Itaq; opposita illa non sunt: nec sequitur; nisi Petrus sit Petra illa, frustra ipsiusmutatum nomen.
units.tr: Reply 1. Far be it from us to say that Christ changed Simon's name and called him Peter in vain and without cause. But it does not follow that he changed it in order to indicate that Peter is the rock upon which he is going to build his Church. Nor does it follow from what Christ promised, that Simon should be called Peter (Joh. 1.45.), nor is it proved from the interpretation of Petra. So those opposed points are not in fact opposed, and it does not follow, unless Peter is that rock, that the changed name was given in vain.

units.la: Quæritur igitur; Quæ causa mutati nominis ? Resp. causam hanc manifeste indigitari, si animadverterimus, Petrum & Petram se habere ut concretum & abstractum, ideoque Petrum denominari à Petra. Verum enim verò cur à Petra Petrus denominetur, dubitatur!
units.tr: The question, therefore, is: what was the cause of the changed name? We reply that the cause is clearly indicated if we notice that Peter and Petra stand to each other as concrete and abstract, and so Peter is named from Petra. But why Peter should be named from Petra is doubtful!

units.la: Resp. Non ideo, quod Petrus Petra sit, à qua denominatur; quemadmodum Christus nō est, qui à Christo Christianus, nec justitia, qui ab illa justus appellatur.
units.tr: We reply: not because Peter is the rock from which he is named, just as Christ is not the one from whom a Christian is called Christian, nor is justice that from which one is called just.

units.la: Sed quia Petram confessus est; vel fide in ea superstructus; vel quia Petram annuntiando super eam ædificavit, ut suprà; vel etiam à constantia, quam Christus ipsi & aliis in solatium contra lapsum hoc ipso promisit. Luc.22.3.32. ut sensus sit. Quia confessus es me Christum filium Dei Viventis, dico tibi, Tu verè es Petrus, & super hanc Petram, quam confessus es, ædificabo te & Universam Ecclesiam meam, ita ut licet Satanas te appetat, quem ventilaret sicut triticum, fides tamen tua non deficiat, sed & alios doctrinâ & exemplo confirmes.
units.tr: But Peter was named so because he confessed the Rock, or because he was built upon it by faith, or because he built upon it by preaching, as above; or also from the steadfastness which Christ promised him, and by this very act promised to others, for their comfort against falling (Luc.22.3.32.). The sense is: "Because you have confessed me to be Christ, the Son of the living God, I say to you: you truly are Peter, and upon this rock which you have confessed I will build you and my whole Church. So although Satan seeks you, to sift you like wheat, your faith will not fail; and you will also strengthen others by your teaching and example."

units.la: Argumentum Pontificiorum huc redit: Cui Christus aliud novum imposuit nomen, is est Petra & fundamentum Ecclesiæ. At Simoni. Ergo. Subsumo sub majore. Abram vocatus à Deo Abraham. Gen. 17. 5. Jacob, Israel. Gen. 32. 28. Filii Zebedæi Boanerges. Marc.3.17. Saulus, Paulus, Act.15.19. Discipuli Christi, Christiani. Act. 11. 26. & Apocal. 2. v.17. promittitur vincenti novum nomen. Quis verò hinc colligat, Ergo hi sunt Petra & fundamentum Ecclesiæ?
units.tr: The argument of the Papists comes to this: "He to whom Christ has given another new name is the rock and foundation of the Church. But Simon was given one. Therefore." I deny the major, pointing to examples: Abram, called Abraham by God (Gen. 17. 5.); Jacob, called Israel (Gen. 32. 28.); the sons of Zebedee, called Boanerges (Marc. 3.17.); Saul, called Paul (Act. 15.19.); Christ's disciples, called Christians (Act. 11. 26.); and in Apoc. 2. v. 17 a new name is promised to the one who conquers. But who would conclude from this: therefore these men are the rock and foundation of the Church?

units.la: Falsa itaque major. Addo nomen Petri non esse excellentius, quàm nomen Christiani, seu novum illud nomen Apocal. 2. v. 17. quo innuitur nomen Filiorum Dei. Nulla igitur inde supra Christianos seu Filios Dei concluditur potestas. Ex his manifestum est, quanquam hoc Petro à Christo dictum sit; nihil tamen dici, quod non etiam alii, inprimis Apostoli, cum ipso commune habeant.
units.tr: The major is therefore false. I add that the name Peter is no more excellent than the name Christian, or the new name of Apoc. 2. v. 17, by which the name of the sons of God is indicated. Therefore no power above Christians or the sons of God follows from it. From these things it is clear that, although this was said to Peter by Christ, nothing is said that others, especially the apostles, do not also share with him.

units.la: At inquiunt, nomen hoc Petrus, proprium, non cum aliis commune & appellativum fuit; nullus enim Apostolorum alius Petrus nominatus: Singularis igitur praerogativa hoc nomine significatur.
units.tr: But they say, this name Peter, was proper, not common and appellative with others; for no other of the apostles Peter was named: therefore a singular pre-eminence is signified by this name.

units.la: Denominativum est à Petra; ergò appellativum, qualia plura alia in omni fere lingua; quæ certæ personæ attributa, usu fiunt propria.
units.tr: It is a denominative from petra, so it is an appellative, like many other words in nearly every language, which become proper names when they are attached to a particular person through usage.

units.la: Nec absurdus forem, si dicerem, cuique fide firmâ prædito nomen Petri tribui posse; quia enim talis instar petræ robustus, firmus & immobilis, adversus quem portæ inferorum non possint prævalere; utpote Christi Petrę illi fundamentali innixus: quid prohibeat, quin Petrum talem appellarem? Præterea cùm Petrus significet lapidem, & quivis verè fidelis, Lapis vivus dicatur i.Petr.2.5. & vers.7. Christus λίθος & πέτρα: ergò & fidelis λίθος & πέτρος [?] cur dici nequeat, non videmus.
units.tr: Nor would I be absurd if I said that the name Petrus could be given to anyone endowed with firm faith. For such a person, like a rock, is robust, firm and immovable, so that the gates of hell cannot prevail against him, being founded upon that foundation stone, Christ. What would prevent me from calling such a person Peter? Moreover, since Petrus means a stone, and every truly faithful person is called a living stone (1 Pet. 2:5, and verse 7 with Christ as lithos and petra), I do not see why the faithful person could not likewise be called lithos and petros [?].

units.la: Posito verò, nomen hoc Petri fuisse proprium, & denotare prærogativam; at tantam, quantam hodierni Pontifices Rom. sibi vendicant, hinc nullâ vel apparente consequentiâ concludi potest.
units.tr: But even granting that this name Peter was proper to him and denoted a pre-eminence, it cannot be concluded from this, with any consequence, even an apparent one, that it was so great a pre-eminence as the present Roman pontiffs claim for themselves.

units.la: Hactenus examinavimus primum & principale argumentum; hocitaq; eviscerato, caetera haud difficulter solvuntur.
units.tr: So far we have examined the first and principal argument. Once this has been disembowelled, the rest are not difficult to solve.

units.la: Secundum argumentum desumitur ex Matth.16.19. tale:
units.tr: The second argument is drawn from Matt. 16:19, and runs thus:

units.la: Cui Christus dedit claves regni cœlorum, &c. est vicarius Christi, caput Ecclesiæ, &c. Atqui Petro dedit Christus claves regni cœlorum, &c. Ergò.
units.tr: Whoever was given by Christ the keys of the kingdom of heaven, etc., is the vicar of Christ, the head of the Church, etc. But Christ gave the keys of the kingdom of heaven, etc., to Peter. Therefore...

units.la: Resp. 1. Major vera non nisi exclusiva; Cui soli dedit,&c.
units.tr: Answer: (1) The major is true only if taken as exclusive: To whom alone he gave, etc.

units.la: 2. Minor verò exclusiva contrariatur his dictis. Matth.18. 8. Joh.20.22.23.
units.tr: (2) The minor, however, when taken as exclusive, is contrary to these passages: Matt. 18:18; John 20:22–23.

units.la: Tertium argumentum ex Joh.21.15.16.17. ita habet:
units.tr: The third argument, from John 21:15–17, runs thus:

units.la: Cui Christus soli tertiâ vice dixit, Pasce oves meas, est Vicarius Christi.
units.tr: The one to whom Christ said alone, for the third time, "Feed my sheep," is the vicar of Christ.

units.la: ℞. 1. Major vera non est: licet enim soli Petro Christus tùm temporis tertiò præceperit, ut oves pascat, minimè tamè ex eo sequitur, quod Pontificii colligunt. Peccat propositio fallaciâ non causæ: alia hujus rei causa; scil. trina Petri abnegatio Christi, quæ iterato hoc mandato tacitè exprobratur; in solatium tamen, ad officiū Apostoli denuò revocatur, & gravi ad constantiâ exhortatione excitatur; quæ omnia Petræ, & fundamēto Ecclesiæ antea constituto parūm conveniunt.
units.tr: Answer: (1) The major is not true. For although Christ then commanded Peter alone, for the third time, to feed his sheep, it by no means follows what the Papists infer from it. The proposition commits the fallacy of a false cause: there is another cause of this matter, namely Peter's threefold denial of Christ, which is tacitly reproached by this repeated command. Yet, for his comfort, he is recalled to the office of an apostle and roused with a grave exhortation to constancy. All of this agrees poorly with Peter as the rock and with the foundation of the Church previously laid.

units.la: 2. Minor verò, quoad præceptum pascendi oves, exclusivè sumpta manifestè falsa est: pugnans cum illo Matt.28.19. & cum praxi non tantum Apostolorum, sed & eorum omnium, qui in Sacra Scriptura Eph.4. Pastores dicuntur.
units.tr: (2) The minor, taken exclusively as to the command to feed the sheep, is manifestly false: it conflicts with Matt. 28:19, and with the practice not only of the apostles but of all those who are called ministers (pastores) in Holy Scripture (Eph. 4).

units.la: 14. Quartum argumentum ex Actor.15. hoc est: Præses Concilii Apostolici est Vicarius Christi, caput Ecclesiæ, &c. Petrus fuit præses, &c. Ergò.
units.tr: 14. The fourth argument, from Acts 15, is this: The president of the apostolic council is the vicar of Christ, the head of the Church, etc. Peter was the president, etc. Therefore...

units.la: ℞. 1. Major nulla est: omne enim Concilii legitimum supra præsidem est, qui nihil aliud concludere potest, nisi quod majoribus suffragiis concluditur.
units.tr: Answer: (1) The major is no good. For every lawful council is above its president, who can conclude nothing except what is concluded by the greater votes.

units.la: 2. Minor ex citato loco concludi nequit.
units.tr: (2) The minor cannot be concluded from the cited passage.

units.la: Hanc verò probant sequentibus:
units.tr: They try to prove this by the following:

units.la: α. Quia Petrus post longam disceptationem sententiam dixit, non principaliter ex S.Scriptura; sed ex revelatione sibi factâ.
units.tr: α. Because Peter, after a long debate, gave his opinion not principally from Holy Scripture, but from a revelation made to him.

units.la: ℞. 1. Si caput, &c. fuisset, non opus fuisset longâ disceptatione, sed citra disputatione sententiæ ipsius subscripsissent.
units.tr: Answer: (1) If he had been the head, etc., there would have been no need for a long debate; they would have subscribed to his opinion without dispute.

units.la: 2. falsum, non principaliter judicasse ex S.Scriptura.
units.tr: (2) It is false that he did not judge principally from Holy Scripture.

units.la: 3. neque enim revelationi fides habita fuisset, nisi ea S.Scripturæ consensisset.
units.tr: (3) For his revelation would not have been believed unless it agreed with Holy Scripture.

units.la: 4. habuit Paulus altiores revelationes; Johannes etiam plures.
units.tr: (4) Paul had higher revelations; John also had many more.

units.la: β. quia Petro à cæteris omnibus fides habita.
units.tr: β. Because Peter was believed by all the others.

units.la: ℞. Etiam Petrus reliquis Apostolis, inprimis Paulo & Barnabæ, fidem habuit. Act.15.12.
units.tr: Answer: Peter also gave credit to the other apostles, above all to Paul and Barnabas (Acts 15:12).

units.la: quia Petrus fuit gentium Apostolus. Actor. 15.7.
units.tr: Because Peter was the apostle of the Gentiles (Acts 15:7).

units.la: Paulus fuit Domino electum instrumentum, ut perferret nomen ipsius in conspectum gentium,& regum,& filiorum Israel. Actor. 9. v.15. Hinc Paulus Galat.2.v.7. ait, concreditum sibi Evangelium praeputii, sicut Petro circumcisionis: & verf.9. cateros Apostolos dextras sibi dedisse & Barnabae, ut ipsi inter gentes, illi vero (non Petrus solus) inter Circumcisos Apostolatu fungerentur.
units.tr: Paul was the chosen instrument of the Lord, to carry his name before the eyes of the Gentiles and of kings and of the sons of Israel (Acts 9:15). Hence Paul says in Gal. 2:7 that the gospel of the uncircumcision had been committed to him, as the gospel of the circumcision was to Peter; and in verse 9 that the other apostles gave the right hand of fellowship to him and Barnabas, so that they should labour among the Gentiles, and the others (not Peter alone) among the circumcised.

units.la: quia Petrus donum miraculorum habuit.
units.tr: Because Peter had the gift of miracles.

units.la: Et caeteri Apostoli habuerunt: Paulus & Barnabas, Actor. 15. 12. Nonnulli qui non sequebantur Christum, etiam multi eo die damnandi. Matth.7.22.23.
units.tr: The other apostles had it too: Paul and Barnabas (Acts 15:12). Many who did not follow Christ, and many on that day, will also be condemned (Matt. 7:22–23).

units.la: quia Petri sententia a Jacobo ex S.Scriptura confirmata.
units.tr: Because Peter's opinion was confirmed from Holy Scripture by James.

units.la: quin ex hoc sequitur
units.tr: Indeed, from this it follows:

units.la: 1. Jacobum potius praesidem fuisse: etenim Postquam Petrus, Paulus item & Barnabas, loquuti essent, omnibus tacentibus, Jacobus ultimo, repetitis iis, quae prolata erant Actor.15. v.13.14. sententiam Simonis (non Petri, non Petrae) ex S.Scriptura confirmavit, verf.15.16.17. Conclusit v.19. 20.21. conclusioni ejus, Apostoli (Petrus quoq;) seniores cum tota Ecclesia subscripserunt, eam denique executioni dederunt, missis quibusda v.25.26.27. Antiochenis scripserunt literas, in quibus haec verba v.28. Visum est Spiritui S. (ecce supremum Judicem & Praesidem) & (non Petro praesidi,no Petro & nobis) sed nobis,sc.concorditer coactis; ut verf.25. id est,toti concilio.
units.tr: (1) That James was rather the president. For after Peter, Paul likewise and Barnabas had spoken, and all were silent, James last, repeating what had been set forth (Acts 15:13–14), confirmed the opinion of Simon (not of Peter, not of Petra) from Holy Scripture (vv. 15–17). He concluded (v. 19–21). To his conclusion the apostles (Peter too), the elders, with the whole Church, subscribed; and finally they put it into execution, sending certain Antiochenes (vv. 25–27) and writing letters, in which these words occur (v. 28): "It seemed good to the Holy Spirit" (behold the supreme Judge and President), and (not to Peter the president, not to Peter and us) "but to us", that is, to those gathered together in agreement; as in verse 25, that is, to the whole council.

units.la: 2. Normam totius controversiae, juxta quam concilium judicabat,fuisse S.Scripturam: quia acta & relata Petri & Pauli ex ea confirmabatur,& juxta eam concludebatur.
units.tr: (2) That the norm of the whole controversy, according to which the council judged, was Holy Scripture, because the acts and reports of Peter and Paul were confirmed from it, and concluded according to it.

units.la: Quintum argumentum ejusmodi est:
units.tr: The fifth argument is of this kind:

units.la: Cui, dum vixit, nullus unquam quaestionem de Primatu movit, is est Vicarius Christi, Caput Ecclesiae,&c.
units.tr: The one against whom, while he lived, no one ever raised a question about the primacy, is the vicar of Christ, the head of the Church, etc.

units.la: Atqui Petro, dum vixit, nullus unquam quaestionem de Primatu movit. Ergo.
units.tr: But no one ever raised a question about the primacy against Peter while he lived. Therefore...

units.la: 1. Major nititur falsâ hypothesi, quæ petit τὸ ἐν ἀρχῇ [?]; Itaque sic limitari debet; Cui habenti Primatum supra omnes reliquos Apostolos & Universam Ecclesiam absolutum, dum vixit, nullus quæstionem movit, is est, &c. absque hac limitatione ridicula est major: limitata verò admittitur. Sed sic
units.tr: (1) The major rests on a false hypothesis, which begs the question (to en archē) [?]. It must therefore be limited thus: The one who, while he lived, had no one raise a question against him, he who had a primacy absolute over all the other apostles and the whole Church, is, etc. Without this limitation the major is ridiculous; with it, it is admitted. But so...

units.la: 2. Minor dupliciter falsa:
units.tr: (2) The minor is false in two ways:

units.la: α. quòd Petrus habuerit talem Primatum:
units.tr: α. That Peter had such a primacy;

units.la: β. nullum unquam, dum vixit Petrus, de eo quæstionem ipsi movisse.
units.tr: β. That no one ever, while Peter lived, raised a question about it against him.

units.la: Quia Christus ipse talem præcellentiam præcidit, ut ex sequentibus patet. Matth.18.1.–4.& c. 20. v. 20.–23. & c. 23. 8. 9. 10. 11. 12. Luc.22. v.24.25.26.27. Joh.13.v.13.–17. His dictis clare satis Christus Primatui Petri contradicit.
units.tr: Because Christ himself cut off such pre-eminence, as is clear from what follows: Matt. 18:1–4, etc.; chap. 20:20–23, etc.; chap. 23:8–12; Luke 22:24–27; John 13:13–17. With these words Christ clearly enough contradicts the primacy of Peter.

units.la: Quia Act. 15. in concilio Hierosolymitano Primatum Petri Apostoli non agnoverunt: constat ex iis, quæ superiùs diximus.
units.tr: Because in the Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15) they did not acknowledge a primacy of Peter the apostle; this is clear from what we said above.

units.la: Quia Paulus, Petro non privatim, sed publicè; nō coram uno aut altero; sed coram omnibus in os restitit. Gal.2. v.11.–14. Nunquam certè hoc fecisset, si Primatum Petri, qualem Pontificii ipsi & Papæ Rom.tribuunt, agnovisset.
units.tr: Because Paul resisted Peter to his face, not privately but publicly, not before one or two but before all (Gal. 2:11–14). He certainly would never have done this if he had acknowledged a primacy of Peter of the kind that the Papists and the Roman pope ascribe to him.

units.la: Quia Petrus ipse talem Primatum in Apostolos nunquam sibi attribuit: patet ex utraque Epistola: nunquam usurpavit, vel exercuit; quod constat ex historia Apostolorum.
units.tr: Because Peter himself never claimed such a primacy over the apostles for himself: this is evident from both Epistles; he never used it or exercised it, as is clear from the history of the apostles.

units.la: 16. Instant tamen, & sextum argumentum adducunt:
units.tr: 16. Yet they press on and bring forward a sixth argument:

units.la: Quem Paulus invisit, & quo cum 14. dies mansit, ut cum eo conferret de suo Apostolatu, eum Paulus agnovit Vicarium Christi, &c. Atqui Petrum Paulus invisit, &c. Ergo.
units.tr: The one whom Paul visited, and with whom he stayed fourteen days, in order to confer with him about his apostleship, Paul acknowledged as the vicar of Christ, etc. But Paul visited Peter, etc. Therefore...

units.la: Major falsa, utpote sub qua infinita absurda subsumi possent.
units.tr: The major is false, since under it infinite absurdities could be subsumed.

units.la: Cætera argumenta omnia extra S. Scripturam adducta, vel ex Patribus, vel ex Conciliis Papisticis desumpta, ceu nimis infirma & humana, jure omitti-
units.tr: We omit, rightly, all the other arguments adduced from outside Holy Scripture, whether taken from the Fathers or from Papistical councils, as too weak and human; and we set Fathers against Fathers and councils against councils.

units.la: mus, & Patres Patribus, Concilia Conciliis opponimus. Hactenus prior propositi pars.
units.tr: So far the first part of our proposition.

units.la: 17. Sequitur altera, sc. Confirmatio Veritatis circa quaestionem propositam: Sufficiet nobis Unicum argumentum, quod brevibus propositum vindicabimus: ita illud habet:
units.tr: 17. There follows the second part, namely the confirmation of the truth concerning the question proposed. One argument will suffice for us, which, once briefly proposed, we shall vindicate. It runs thus:

units.la: Aut Christus Filius Dei Viventis solus est Petra illa, supra quam aedificat Ecclesiam: aut praeter illum est etiam alius.
units.tr: Either Christ, the Son of the living God, alone is that rock upon which he builds the Church, or there is besides him also another.

units.la: At solus Christus Filius Dei viventis est Petra illa, &c. Ergo praeter illum nemo alius.
units.tr: But Christ alone, the Son of the living God, is that rock, etc. Therefore besides him no one else.

units.la: Major est extra omnem Controversiam.
units.tr: The major is beyond all controversy.

units.la: Minorem probamus
units.tr: We prove the minor:

units.la: 1. Ex antecedentibus; id est, ex confessione Petri: Quem Petrus ex revelatione Dei confessus est, ille solus est Petra illa supra quam, &c.
units.tr: (1) From the preceding: that is, from Peter's confession. The one whom Peter confessed by a revelation from God is alone that rock upon which, etc.

units.la: Atqui Christus Filius Dei viventis est quem Petrus ex revelatione Dei Patris confessus est. Ergo
units.tr: But Christ is the Son of the living God, whom Peter confessed from the revelation of God the Father. Therefore:

units.la: Majorem probo:
units.tr: I prove the major premise:

units.la: A quo Petrus denominatus Petrus, ille solus est Petra supra quam, &c.
units.tr: That one, from whom Peter was named Peter, alone is the Rock upon which, etc.

units.la: Atqui ab illo, quem Petrus ex revelatione Dei Patris confessus est, denominatus est Petrus. Ergo.
units.tr: But Peter was named Peter from him whom he confessed from the revelation of God the Father. Therefore:

units.la: Utraque praemissarum manifesta est ex Matth. 16. tum ex dictis, & porro dicendis.
units.tr: Each of the premises is plain from Matthew 16, as much from what has been said as from what is yet to be said.

units.la: 2. Ex ipsis his verbis: Et supra hanc Petram aedificabo Ecclesiam meam, & portae inferorum non praevalebunt ei.
units.tr: 2. From these very words: And upon this Rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

units.la: a. à nomine Petra: hoc praesuppositio, intelligi Petram non Corporalem, sed Spiritualem; quod in controversia erat.
units.tr: a. From the name Rock: it is presupposed that the Rock is to be understood not as corporeal but as spiritual, which was the point in dispute.

units.la: 1. Ex ipsa voce sic:
units.tr: 1. From the word itself, thus:

units.la: In universa S.Scriptura nemo alius dicitur Petra, scil. Spiritualis, quam Christus Filius Dei viventis. Deut. 32. 4. 2. Sam. 2. 2. Psalm. 18. 2. Es. 8. 14. Rom. 9. 33. 1. Cor. 10. 4. 1. Pet. 2. 8.
units.tr: In all of Holy Scripture no one else is called a Rock, that is, a spiritual Rock, except Christ, the Son of the living God. Deut. 32.4. 2 Sam. 2.2. Ps. 18.2. Isa. 8.14. Rom. 9.33. 1 Cor. 10.4. 1 Pet. 2.8.

units.la: Solus itaque Christus, Filius ille Dei viventis, est Petra illa, &c.
units.tr: Christ alone, therefore, that Son of the living God, is that Rock, etc.

units.la: 2. Ex Synonymis
units.tr: 2. From synonyms.

units.la: α. Ratione vocis:
units.tr: α. By reason of the word:

units.la: 1. Qui est imus angularis lapis electus, pretiosus, caput anguli, lapis offendiculi & Petra offensionis, ille solus est Petra illa supra quam,&c.
units.tr: He who is the chief corner stone, chosen, precious, the head of the corner, the stone of stumbling and the Rock of offence, he alone is that Rock upon which, etc.

units.la: Atqui Christus, Filius Dei viventis, est imus,&c. Ephes. 2.20. 1.Petr.2.6.7. Esa.28.16. Ergò,&c.
units.tr: But Christ, the Son of the living God, is the chief corner stone, etc. Eph. 2.20. 1 Pet. 2.6, 7. Isa. 28.16. Therefore, etc.

units.la: 2. Qui est fundamentum Ecclesiæ, præter quod nemo aliud potest ponere, ille solus est Petra illa, supra quam,&c.
units.tr: He who is the foundation of the Church, besides which no one else can lay another, he alone is that Rock upon which, etc.

units.la: Atqui Christus Filius Dei viventis, est fundamentum illud,&c. 1.Cor.3.11. Ephes.2.20. Ergo,&c.
units.tr: But Christ the Son of the living God is that foundation, etc. 1 Cor. 3.11. Eph. 2.20. Therefore, etc.

units.la: β. Ratione rei. Etenim ille est imus angularis lapis, fundamentum, adeoque Petra Ecclesiæ supra quam,&c. Qui est Messias, Mediator inter Deum & homines, Redemptor, Dominus, caput Ecclesiæ, Propheta, Summus, Sacerdos & Pontifex secundum ordinem Melchisedek, Rex Sionis, Sponsus Ecclesiæ, solus habens nomen sub cœlo supra omne nomen,&c.
units.tr: β. By reason of the thing. For he is the chief corner stone and the foundation, and so the Rock of the Church upon which, etc. He who is the Messiah, the Mediator between God and men, the Redeemer, the Lord, the head of the Church, the Prophet, the High Priest and Priest after the order of Melchizedek, the King of Zion, the Bridegroom of the Church, who alone has a name under heaven above every name, etc.

units.la: Hæc vero singula seorsim,& omnia simul, de solo D.N.J.Christo, Filio Dei viventis,in S.Scriptura dicuntur.
units.tr: These things, taken singly and all together, are said in Holy Scripture of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God, alone.

units.la: 3. Ex ædificatione Ecclesiæ; ita enim Christus ait: Et super hanc Petram ædificabo Ecclesiam meam, ubi vox Ædificabo, per metaphoram duo indicat, ex quibus firmissima argumenta educuntur:
units.tr: 3. From the building of the Church; for thus Christ says: And upon this Rock I will build my Church, where the word "I will build" indicates two things by metaphor, from which the firmest arguments are drawn:

units.la: α. Prius est ædificatio, seu exstructio operis, seu Ecclesiæ: cujus causa prima est SS.Trinitas.
units.tr: α. The first is the building, or construction of the work, or of the Church, whose first cause is the Holy Trinity.

units.la: Architectus, Dominus noster Jesus Christus, qui dicit ædificabo.
units.tr: The architect is our Lord Jesus Christ, who says "I will build."

units.la: Hunc enim Deus Pater præordinavit ante jacta mundi fundamenta, 1. Petr. 1.20. in Hoc, ceu fundamento, ædificandos elegit, Ephes. 1. 4. huic eosdem dedit, Joh.17.6,&c. hunc in tempore misit.Galat. 4.4.hunc pro nobis dedit, Joh. 3. 16. hunc audiendum cœlitus monuit, Matth.17.
units.tr: For God the Father foreordained him before the foundations of the world were laid (1 Pet. 1.20); in him, as in a foundation, he chose those to be built (Eph. 1.4); he gave them to him (John 17.6, etc.); he sent him in time (Gal. 4.4); he gave him for us (John 3.16); he commanded from heaven that he be heard (Matt. 17).

units.la: Hic D.N.J.C., ædificavit ut Propheta doctrinâ suâ,non alterius,ut Sacerdos merito suo, ut Rex efficaciâ & virtute suâ.
units.tr: Here our Lord Jesus Christ built: as Prophet, by his own teaching and not another's; as Priest, by his own merit; as King, by his own efficacy and power.

units.la: Operarii ; Primarius Spiritus S. Spiritus ille Christi, de quo Christus Joh.16.14,15. & Paulus 1.Cor.12.11.
units.tr: The workmen: the chief is the Holy Spirit, that Spirit of Christ, concerning whom Christ speaks (John 16.14, 15), and Paul (1 Cor. 12.11).

units.la: Administri hujus sunt Prophetae, Apostoli, horumque legitimi successores, servi Christi, ministri Spiritus, qui omnes nullum aliud fundamentum posuerunt praeter id, quod positum est, quod est Jesus Christus, 1.Cor.3.11.
units.tr: The ministers of this work are the Prophets, the Apostles and their lawful successors, servants of Christ, ministers of the Spirit, who all laid no other foundation than that which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ (1 Cor. 3.11).

units.la: Instrumenta seu media sunt Verbum (Lex & Evangelium) & Sacramenta; quorum Nucleus non alius, quam Christus, Act.10.43. 1.Cor.2.2. Galat. 6.14. &c. ad quem, ceu ad rem significatam & signatam, nos remittunt.
units.tr: The instruments or means are the Word (Law and Gospel) and the Sacraments; whose kernel is none other than Christ (Acts 10.43; 1 Cor. 2.2; Gal. 6.14, etc.), to whom they refer us as to the thing signified and sealed.

units.la: Materia sunt Lapides; nempe
units.tr: The material is stones, namely:

units.la: Imus ille angularis, electus & pretiosus lapis, &c. 1.Pet.2.6,7
units.tr: That chief corner stone, chosen and precious, etc. 1 Pet. 2.6, 7.

units.la: Caeteri vivi & electi lapides super Imum illum aedificandi.1.Pet.2.5. Eph.2.20,21,22.
units.tr: The other living and chosen stones, to be built upon that chief stone. 1 Pet. 2.5. Eph. 2.20, 21, 22.

units.la: Forma operationis est modus, quo lapides illi, in se dispersi, Imo illi Lapidi, Petrae & Fundamento, superaedificantur.
units.tr: The form of the operation is the manner in which those stones, scattered in themselves, are built up upon that very Stone, Rock and Foundation.

units.la: Hic consistit
units.tr: This consists

units.la: In genere, in unitione & conjunctione cum Christo, Johan.17.20,21.
units.tr: In general, in union and conjunction with Christ. John 17.20, 21.

units.la: In specie vero est
units.tr: In particular it is:

units.la: Vocatio & tractio ad Christum. Joh. 6.44,45,65.
units.tr: The calling and drawing to Christ. John 6.44, 45, 65.

units.la: Justificatio per fidem in Christum. Rom.4.5. &c.
units.tr: Justification by faith in Christ. Rom. 4.5, etc.

units.la: Adoptio in Christo. Gal.4. 5,6,7.
units.tr: Adoption in Christ. Gal. 4.5, 6, 7.

units.la: Vivificatio & sanctificatio in Christo & per Christum. Gal.2.20. 1.Cor.15.22. Joh.15. 2,3,4,5. Joh.17.19.
units.tr: Quickening and sanctification in Christ and through Christ. Gal. 2.20. 1 Cor. 15.22. John 15.2, 3, 4, 5. John 17.19.

units.la: Perseverantia & mansio in Christo. Joh. 6.56. & c. 10. verf.28,29.
units.tr: Perseverance and abiding in Christ. John 6.56, etc.; ch. 10 vv. 28, 29.

units.la: Salvatio in Christo, extra quem salus nulla est. Act.4. verf.12.
units.tr: Salvation in Christ, outside whom there is no salvation. Acts 4 v. 12.

units.la: Forma operis seu aedificii hujus
units.tr: The form of this work or building is:

units.la: Externa, est Evangelii Jesu Christi annuntiatio, & Sacramentorum ab eodem in memoriam mortis suae institu-torum administratio. Matth.28.19,20. Marc.16.16. 1.Cor.11.24,25,26. &c.
units.tr: The external form is the proclamation of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, and the administration of the Sacraments instituted by him in memory of his death. Matt. 28.19, 20. Mark 16.16. 1 Cor. 11.24, 25, 26, etc.

units.la: Interna est mutua omnium vivorum lapidum, id est, fidelium, cum Imo lapide seu Petra, nempe Christo, & inter se, unio mystica & arctissima.
units.tr: The internal form is the mutual, mystical and most intimate union of all the living stones, that is, of the faithful, with the chief stone or Rock, namely Christ, and with one another.

units.la: Finis, est glorificatio Dei Patris in & per Christum. Joh. 17.4.&c. & salus unitorum Christo aeterna. Joh. 6. v. 54, 55, 56.
units.tr: The end is the glorification of God the Father in and through Christ (John 17.4, etc.) and the eternal salvation of those united to Christ (John 6 vv. 54, 55, 56).

units.la: Singula haec totidem sunt argumenta, quibus evidentissimè probatur; solum D. N. J. Christum esse Petram Ecclesiae.
units.tr: Each of these is as many arguments by which it is most evidently proved that our Lord Jesus Christ alone is the Rock of the Church.

units.la: Alterum est Ædificium ipsum, id est Ecclesia. Haec non est alius, quàm Christi; quod non tantum exmodò dictis palàm est: sed maximè, quòd ipsi ut Petrae innixa, supra ipsum superstructa, ab ipso & in ipso conservetur, ut jure dicat; Supra hanc Petram, id est, supra me aedificabo Ecclesiam, non alterius, sed meam. Quae causa est, quòd eadem Ecclesia non ab humano nomine, non à Petro Petrina, Paulina à Paulo; minùs à Papa Papana, à Luthero Lutherana, à Zuinglio & Calvino, Zuingliana aut Calviniana; sed à Christo Christiana denominari debeat, ut omnis gloria Uni Christo sarta tecta conservetur. 1.Cor.3. v.4,5,&c.
units.tr: The other is the building itself, that is, the Church. This is none other than Christ's; which is clear not only from what has been said, but chiefly because it is sustained by him as its Rock, built up on him as its superstructure, and preserved by him and in him; so that he may rightly say: Upon this Rock, that is, upon me, I will build the Church, not of another, but my. For this reason the same Church ought to be named not from a human name: not Petrine from Peter, Pauline from Paul; still less Papal from the Pope, Lutheran from Luther, Zwinglian or Calvinian from Zwingli and Calvin; but Christian from Christ, so that all glory may be kept safe and whole for the One Christ (1 Cor. 3 vv. 4, 5, etc.).

units.la: Ab Ecclesiae officio: unde prodit tale collectivum argumentum; Ecclesia, & in ea quivis verè fidelis Solius Christi vocem ex mandato Patris coelestis Mat.17. v.5. audit, eumque solum sequitur. Johan. 8. v. 12. Joh.10. v.27.&c.
units.tr: From the office of the Church, whence arises this collective argument: the Church, and in it any truly faithful person, hears the voice of Christ alone by the command of the heavenly Father (Matt. 17 v. 5), and follows him alone (John 8 v. 12; John 10 v. 27, etc.).

units.la: Firmâ fide, vivâ spe & sincerâ charitate, soli Christo innititur, manet in ipso & perseverat ad finem: à Christo petit & expectat omnia salutaria dona; salutem & vitam aeternam; certus, illum solum viam, veritatem & vitâ, sine quo ad Patrem pervenire nemo possit, Joh.14. 6. esse resurrectionem & vitam. Joh.11.25,26. Ergo solum Christum credit esse Petram suam.
units.tr: With firm faith, living hope and sincere love, it leans on Christ alone, abides in him and perseveres to the end; it seeks and expects from Christ all saving gifts, salvation and eternal life; certain that he alone is the way, the truth and the life, without whom no one can come to the Father (John 14.6), and that he is the resurrection and the life (John 11.25, 26). Therefore it believes that Christ alone is its Rock.

units.la: Ab Ecclesiae defensione: quae indicatur his: Et porta inferorum non superabunt eam.
units.tr: From the defence of the Church, which is indicated by these words: And the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

units.la: In quo, à quo & per quem Ecclesia ita confirmatur & conservatur, ut ne quidem portae inferorum, id est, omnes omnium Diabolorum totiusque mundi insidiae & potentiae, Ecclesiae praevalere possint, ille solus est Petra illa, &c. patet ex Matth.7.24.
units.tr: In whom, by whom and through whom the Church is so confirmed and preserved that not even the gates of hell, that is, all the snares and powers of all the devils and of the whole world, can prevail against the Church: he alone is that Rock, etc. This is plain from Matt. 7.24.

units.la: Atqui in Christo Filio Dei viventis, ab illo & per illum ita confirmatur & confervatur Ecclesia: probo:
units.tr: But in Christ the Son of the living God the Church is so confirmed and preserved, by him and through him. I prove it:

units.la: Sicut enim Christus, ut ab omni malo liberaret Ecclesiam, perpessione pœnæ, peccatum, mundum, mortem, Diabolum, gehennam superavit; Utq; vitā æternā omniaq; cœlestia dona Ecclesiæ acquireret, legem Dei plenè & perfectè ejus loco præstitit: Ita quotquot verā fide in ipso radicati sunt, eos servat, ut nemo pereat, nemo è manibus ipsius auferatur, sed det eis vitam æternam. Joh.3.16. Joh.6. &c c.10.27. &c.
units.tr: For just as Christ, in order to free the Church from every evil, overcame by the endurance of punishment sin, the world, death, the Devil and hell; and in order to acquire for the Church eternal life and all heavenly gifts, fulfilled the law of God fully and perfectly in its place; so he keeps all who are rooted in him by true faith, so that none perishes, none is snatched out of his hands, but he gives them eternal life (John 3.16; John 6, etc.; ch. 10.27, etc.).

units.la: 6. Ex dato ministerio clavium sic concludimus;
units.tr: 6. From the ministry of the keys given, we conclude thus:

units.la: Qui dat, Petro quidem nominatim, omnibus quoque reliquis Apostolis, horumque legitimis successoribus, claves regni cœlorum, ut quicquid ligaverint in terra, sit ligatum in cœlis, & quicquid solverint in terra, solutum sit in cœlis, ille solus est Petra, supra quam, &c.
