units.tr: He who gives the keys of the kingdom of heaven, to Peter by name, and likewise to all the other Apostles and their lawful successors, so that whatever they bind on earth is bound in heaven, and whatever they loose on earth is loosed in heaven, he alone is the Rock upon which, etc.

units.la: Rationes hujus propositionis sunt:
units.tr: The reasons for this proposition are these:

units.la: 1. Qui talia dat, eum necesse est, non tantum habere quod dat; sed etiam habere potestatem dandi ea etiam aliis.
units.tr: 1. He who gives such things must not only have what he gives, but must also have the power of giving them to others.

units.la: Imò eum oportet habere potestatem non solum in terra; sed etiam in cœlis, ejus, quod secundum voluntatem ipsius faciunt, quibus dat claves; unde non simpliciter nominat Claves, sed Claves Regni cœlorum. Ex quo consequitur, talem habere summam potestatem, totius regni cœlorum administrationem humeris ipsius incumbere, ac proin Petram esse, quæ totam Ecclesiam sustineat & conservet.
units.tr: Indeed, he must have power not only on earth but also in heaven, over what they do according to his will, to whom he gives the keys. Hence he does not simply say "keys" but "keys of the kingdom of heaven." From this it follows that such a one has supreme power, that the administration of the whole kingdom of heaven rests on his shoulders, and therefore that he is the Rock which sustains and preserves the whole Church.

units.la: 2. Magnum discrimen est inter eum, qui dat, & inter eum, qui accipit. Dat enim Dominus claves regni cœlorum: accipiunt Servi, qui absq; voluntate Domini eas aliis dare non possunt.
units.tr: 2. There is a great difference between him who gives and him who receives. The Lord gives the keys of the kingdom of heaven; servants receive them, and they cannot give them to others without the Lord's will.

units.la: Habet itaq; Dominus dans supremam potestatem & absolutā, ad rationes dandas nemini obnoxius: qui verò accipiunt, habent potestatem circumscriptam, nec eam pro lubitu, sed juxta voluntatem & imperium Domini exercere,deniq; Domino rationes officii reddere debent. Penes dantem est potestas & imperium, accipienti incumbit officium & ministerium.
units.tr: Therefore the Lord who gives has supreme and absolute power, answerable to no one for his reasons. Those who receive have limited power, and may not exercise it as they please but according to the will and command of the Lord, and in the end they must render an account of their office to the Lord. Power and command rest with the giver; office and ministry belong to the receiver.

units.la: Atqui Christus Filius Dei viventis, est qui dat claves regni coelorum. Matth.16.19. nominatim Petro, ibid.
units.tr: But Christ, the Son of the living God, is the one who gives the keys of the kingdom of heaven: Matt. 16.19. To Peter by name, ibid.

units.la: sed & in Petro & cum Petro caeteris Apostolis horumq; successoribus legitimis. Confer cum eo quod Matth. 16.19. habetur, id, quod legitur Matth.18.18. Joh. 20. 22,23. Idem probat praxis Apostolorum & Successorum in hunc usque diem.
units.tr: But also in Peter, and with Peter the other apostles and their lawful successors. Compare with what is said at Matt. 16.19 what is read at Matt. 18.18 and John 20.22, 23. The practice of the apostles and their successors down to this day proves the same.

units.la: Ergo solus Christus est Petra illa,&c.
units.tr: Therefore Christ alone is that Rock, etc.

units.la: Ex dictis liquet, haec ipsa verba, ex quibus Pontificii Primatum Petri adstruere conantur, evidentissime eundem destruere, & soli Christo tribuere.
units.tr: From what has been said it is clear that these very words, from which the Papists try to establish the primacy of Peter, most evidently overthrow it and ascribe it to Christ alone.

units.la: Sequitur Vindicatio nostri argumenti. Excipiunt adversarii distinguendo Inter Petram.fundamentum & Caput,&c.
units.tr: There follows the vindication of our argument. The adversaries except, by distinguishing "between the Rock, foundation and Head," etc.

units.la: 1. Principale & subordinatum seu ministeriale.
units.tr: 1. Principal and subordinate, or ministerial.

units.la: 2. Invisibile & Visibile.
units.tr: 2. Invisible and visible.

units.la: 3. Praesens in coelo & in terra.
units.tr: 3. Present in heaven and on earth.

units.la: Docent, Christum solum esse Petram, fundamentum & Caput,&c. principale, invisibile, praesens in coelo. Petrum vero & Successores esse ministeriale, visibile, praesens in terris.
units.tr: They teach that Christ alone is the Rock, foundation and Head, etc., principal, invisible, present in heaven; but Peter and his successors are ministerial, visible, present on earth.

units.la: Ad has vero distinctiones respondemus, esse eas,
units.tr: To these distinctions we reply as follows:

units.la: I. Ἀ̓γράφως[?]. Etenim fundantur vel in locis praecedenti ἀναγνωστικῇ[?] aut καταγνωστικῇ[?] citatis: vel in aliis S.Scripturae locis.
units.tr: I. They are unscriptural [agraphōs]. For they are founded either on the passages cited above, which have been examined, or on other passages of Holy Scripture.

units.la: At vero nec in citatis & examinatis locis ullum esse harum distinctionum fundamentum, palam fecimus: nec ex aliis Scripturae testimoniis probari possunt. Sunt igitur ἄγραφοι.
units.tr: But we have made it plain that there is no foundation for these distinctions in the cited and examined passages, and they cannot be proved from other testimonies of Scripture. They are therefore unscriptural.

units.la: At, inquiunt, in V.T. praeter Christum fuisse Summum Sacerdotem Aaronem ejusq; Successores: ergo & in N.T. praeter Christum esse Petrum ejusq; Successores.
units.tr: But, they say, in the Old Testament there was, besides Christ, Aaron the high priest and his successors; therefore in the New Testament there is, besides Christ, Peter and his successors.

units.la: [?]. 1. Summus Sacerdos in V.T. typus fuit Petræ, id est, Christi non Petri, &c.
units.tr: 1. The high priest in the Old Testament was a type of the Rock, that is, of Christ, not of Peter, etc.

units.la: 2. Cùm jam venerit, qui illo & aliis typis adumbratus est; Christum in carnem venisse negat, & est AntiChristus, negans Patrem & Filium, quisquis præter Christum alium Summum Sacerdotem statuit.
units.tr: 2. Since he has now come who was foreshadowed by that and other types, whoever denies that Christ has come in the flesh is an Antichrist, denying the Father and the Son; and so is whoever sets up another high priest besides Christ.

units.la: 2. Ἀντιγραφὰς[?]: hoc manifestum est
units.tr: 2. Contradictory [antigraphas]. This is manifest:

units.la: α. Ex argumentis nostris, quibus ex Matth. 16. evidentissimè probavimus, solum Christum, Filium Dei viventis, esse Petram illam, supra quam, &c. Huic contradicit, qui duas distinctas Petras, duo distincta fundamenta statuit.
units.tr: α. From our arguments, by which from Matt. 16 we most evidently proved that Christ alone, the Son of the living God, is that Rock upon which, etc. Whoever sets up two distinct Rocks and two distinct foundations contradicts this.

units.la: β. Contradicunt hæ distinctiones ipsi Petro. In genere: Petrus in suis epistolis nullibi ullius mentionem facit; vel Petræ vel Capitis, &c. nisi Christi.
units.tr: β. These distinctions contradict Peter himself. In general: Peter nowhere in his epistles mentions anyone as Rock or Head, etc., except Christ.

units.la: In specie. 1. Epist. c. 2. v. 6. 7. Solum Christum appellat Lapidem in Sion in imo angulo, electum, pretiosum, cui qui credit, non pudefiet, quem reprobaverunt ædificantes, factum caput anguli, lapidem offendiculi, & Petram offensionis, & cap.5.[?]v.1. se non vocat Petram supra quam, &c. sed συμπρεσβύτερον[?] & confortem gloriæ patefaciendæ.
units.tr: In particular: 1 Pet. 2.6, 7: he calls only Christ the stone in Zion, chosen, precious, in the chief corner, whoever believes in him shall not be put to shame, whom the builders rejected, made the head of the corner, a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence. And at 5.1 he does not call himself the Rock upon which, etc., but a fellow-elder [symprebyteros] and a partaker in the glory to be revealed.

units.la: v.2. nō sibi soli dicit concreditum munus pascendi, sed συμπρεσβυτέρης hortatur, Pascite gregem, &c.
units.tr: v.2: he does not say that the charge of feeding is entrusted to himself alone, but as a fellow-elder he exhorts: Feed the flock, etc.

units.la: v.3. ait: neq; ut dominantes Clero, &c.
units.tr: v.3: he says: nor as lording it over the clergy, etc.

units.la: v.4. Christo soli tribuit titulum ἀρχιποίμενος[?], &c.
units.tr: v.4: he attributes to Christ alone the title of chief shepherd [archipoimēn], etc.

units.la: Ex quibus sic arguo; Aut Petrus fuit supra reliquos Presbyteros & clerum, caput & Dominus: aut non fuit: At non prius: secus sibi, imò Domino constituenti ipsum caput & Dominum, cōtradixisset, quod inconveniens: ergo posterius. Itaque Petrus contradicit Pontificiis; & hi illi, adeoq; S. Scripturæ.
units.tr: From these points I argue thus: either Peter was above the rest of the elders and the clergy, head and lord, or he was not. But not the former: otherwise he would have contradicted himself, and indeed the Lord who appointed him head and lord, which is absurd. Therefore the latter. Thus Peter contradicts the Papists; and they contradict him, and so Holy Scripture.

units.la: γ. Porrò sic argumentor:
units.tr: γ. Furthermore, I argue thus:

units.la: Qui aliud Evangelium evangelizat, præter id, quod Paulus, Petrus, aliúsve Apostolus evangelizavit, is est anathema contradicens S. Scripturæ. At, qui aliud fundamentum Ecclesiæ ponit præter id, quod positum est, quod est Christus Jesus, is aliud Evangelium evangelizat præter id, quod evangelizavit Petrus, Paulus, aliúsve Apostolus. Ergò : concludant Pontificii.
units.tr: He who preaches another gospel, besides that which Paul, Peter or another apostle preached, is anathema, contradicting Holy Scripture. But he who lays down another foundation of the Church besides that which has been laid, which is Christ Jesus, preaches another gospel besides that which Peter, Paul or another apostle preached. Therefore, let the Papists draw the conclusion.

units.la: [?]. Cœlestis Legislator præcepto primo dicit: Non erit tibi Deus alius coram me: quia unus Deus: ita quia unus Mediator, Petra & caput Ecclesiæ: non erit tibi alius præter me, jure merito Christus requirit: nam ut unus Deus: ita unus Mediator inter Deum & homines est Christus. 1.Tim.2.5.
units.tr: [?] The heavenly Lawgiver says in the first precept: You shall have no other God before me, because there is one God. So, because there is one Rock and Head of the Church, rightly Christ requires: you shall have no other besides me. For as there is one God, so there is one Mediator between God and men, Christ. 1 Tim. 2.5.

units.la: 3. Ἀλόγως[?]. Hoc demonstrari posset per omnes artes liberales, per omnia causarum genera Rhetorica, per Logicæ inventionis argumenta universa, per mille absurda; posset ob oculos poni cæcis, modò cæci essent;&c.
units.tr: 3. Absurdly [alogōs]. This could be demonstrated by all the liberal arts, by every kind of rhetorical argument, by all the arguments of logical invention, by a thousand absurdities; it could be set before the eyes of the blind, if only they were blind; etc.

units.la: Duobus verò tantum argumentis harum distinctionum vanitatem ostendam.
units.tr: I shall show the vanity of these distinctions by two arguments only.

units.la: α. Non diffitebuntur adversarii
units.tr: α. The adversaries will not deny

units.la: 1. Synonima esse Ecclesiæ Petram, imum angularem lapidem, fundamentum, Caput, Christum, Mediatorem, Redemptorem, Regem, Pastorem animarum, Sponsum,&c. hæc enim de se invicem prædicari posse, certū est.
units.tr: 1. That the Rock of the Church, the chief corner stone, foundation, Head, Christ, Mediator, Redeemer, King, Shepherd of souls, Bridegroom, etc. are synonyms; for it is certain that these can be predicated of one another.

units.la: 2. Esse hæc omnia vocabula relativa, quorū correlatū est Ecclesia, aliter atq; aliter à relato denominata.
units.tr: 2. That all these words are relative, whose correlate is the Church, and are named differently according to what they are related to.

units.la: 3. Ecclesiam collectivè sumptam esse unam.
units.tr: 3. That the Church, taken collectively, is one.

units.la: His positis sumatur ex nominibus Ecclesiæ correlatis quodcunq;, evidentissimum absurdum consequetur: Quis enim ausit dicere, Ecclesiæ,ut ædificii,esse duas Petras, fundamenta duo, imos angulares lapides duos? Ecclesiæ, ut redemptæ, esse duos Redemptores, ut regni cœlorum, esse duos Reges, corporis, esse duo capita, sponsæ, duos esse Sponsos, unum scil. principale alterum ministerialem; Invisibilem visibilem; in cœlis, in terris.
units.tr: With these points laid down, whatever is drawn from the correlative names of the Church, the most evident absurdity will follow. For who would dare to say that the Church, as a building, has two rocks, two foundations, two chief corner stones? That the Church, as redeemed, has two Redeemers; as the kingdom of heaven, two Kings; as a body, two heads; as a bride, two bridegrooms, namely one principal and the other ministerial; one invisible and one visible; one in heaven and one on earth?

units.la: Implicant hæc multis modis:
units.tr: These distinctions entangle the matter in many ways:

units.la: 1. In genere : Etenim hæ distinctiones impingunt in omnes bonæ distributionis regulas: & perinde se habent, ac si quis distingueret Unum, in unum & unum, id est, non unum sed multa : Caput in caput & caput, id est, capita ; imò Ens, in ens & non ens. Ex S.Scriptura namque evicimus, Petram illam, supra quam ędificatur[?] Ecclesia,esse Individuum & Singulare: ideoque non posse aliis numero distinctis attribui: hoc enim speciērum est : Quemadmodum Sol, quia unus est, non potest distingui in Principalem & ministerialem, visibilem & invisibilem, &c. ita Beatæ Virginis Filius unus est, ideoque hoc nomen, sub nulla distinctione, pluribus tribui potest.
units.tr: 1. In general: these distinctions run against all the rules of sound division. They are just as if someone should distinguish One into one and one, that is, not one but many; or Head into head and head, that is, heads; or indeed Being into being and non-being. For from Holy Scripture we have shown that the Rock upon which the Church is built is individual and singular, and therefore cannot be attributed to other things distinct in number, since that belongs to species. Just as the Sun, because it is one, cannot be divided into principal and ministerial, visible and invisible, etc., so the Son of the Blessed Virgin is one, and therefore this name cannot be given to several under any distinction.

units.la: Nullâ quoque legitimâ distinctione unum Correlatum, in se & correlatum distingui potest: ex. gr. Rex singularis, in Regem & Subditum : neq; correlatum aut correlati membrum singulare, nomen recipit correlati: ex. gr. Membrum corporis aut totū corpus,non potest dici Caput: minimè Sponsa appellari Sponsus: Christus est caput, Petrus est membrum: Sponsus: Sponsa seu membrum Sponsæ. Dominus Minister ex multis unus; Itaq; nomen Christi Petro tribui nequit: hoc autè faciunt distinctiones dictæ.
units.tr: Likewise, no correlate can be distinguished, in itself and as a correlate, by any lawful distinction: e.g. a single king cannot be divided into King and Subject. Nor does a singular correlate, or a singular member of a correlate, receive the name of the correlate: e.g. a member of the body, or the whole body, cannot be called Head; by no means can the Bride be called Bridegroom. Christ is head, Peter is a member; Bridegroom, Bride, or member of the Bride. The Lord Minister is one out of many; therefore the name of Christ cannot be given to Peter. Yet the aforesaid distinctions do exactly this.

units.la: Ratio : quia Caput hoc, Sponsus hic, Dominus iste, non est species, sed individuum & relatum singulare.
units.tr: The reason: this Head, this Bridegroom, this Lord, is not a species but an individual and a singular correlative.

units.la: Omne autem distributum, Species sive univoca sive analoga esse debet.
units.tr: Now whatever is distributed must be a species, whether univocal or analogous.

units.la: Denique cum Petra hæc non minus sit singularissima atq; Deus seu Dei essentia. 1.Tim.2.5.[?] & præter hanc nulla alia esse possit ; sicut nec præter Deum alius est, necesse est alterum distributionis hujus membrum esse non ens: non minus enim Petra hæc distingui potest in Petram principalem & ministerialem, atque Ens in ens verum & fictum sive non ens.
units.tr: Finally, since this Rock is no less singular than God, or the essence of God (1 Tim. 2.5 [?]), and since no other can exist besides it, just as no other exists besides God, it follows that one member of this distinction must be a non-being. For this Rock can no more be divided into a principal and a ministerial Rock than Being can be divided into true being and fictitious being, or non-being.

units.la: In specie
units.tr: In particular:

units.la: 1. Petra, fundamentum vel Caput ministeriale, involvit contradictionem. Dicit enim Petram non Petram,&c. quod ex Synonimis clarius liquet: Quid enim absurdius, quàm dicere Dominum, Regem, Christum, Sponsum ministerialem?
units.tr: 1. A ministerial Rock, foundation, or Head involves a contradiction. For it calls a Rock not a Rock, and so on, which is made clearer by the synonyms. For what is more absurd than to speak of a ministerial Lord, King, Christ, or Bridegroom?

units.la: Equidem verè dicere possumus, Ministrum Domini, Regis, Christi, Sponsi; sed Ministerialem Dominum, inauditum est & ἀλογον.
units.tr: Indeed we can truly speak of a minister of the Lord, King, Christ, or Bridegroom; but a ministerial Lord is unheard of and [ἄλογον, unreasonable].

units.la: Porrò Petra illa, supra quam Christus aedificat Ecclesiam suam, aut sufficiens est ad sustentandum & corroborandum aedificium, aut non est sufficiens: Hoc verò derogat gloriae Christi: si verò illud, nulla est ministerialis Petrae &c. necesitas. Quòd in aedificanda Ecclesia ministrorum operâ utitur, hoc non de necesitate est sui respectu; sed nostri tantum respectu: ipse enim horum operâ facile carere posset; siquidem hi ex se nihil possunt, sed quicquid agunt, id coelitus datur. Hinc Paulus (non minor Petro) 1.Cor.3.5.6.7. Quis est Paulus, quis Apollo, nisi ministri, per quos credidistis, & ut cuiq; Dominus dedit? Ego plantavi, Apollos rigavit: sed Deus dedit incrementum: Itaq; neq; is qui plantat, est aliquid, neq; is qui rigat, sed Deus qui dat incrementum.
units.tr: Moreover, that Rock upon which Christ builds his Church is either sufficient to support and strengthen the building, or it is not. The latter derogates from the glory of Christ; if the former, then there is no necessity for a ministerial Rock, and so on. That he uses the work of ministers in building the Church is not necessary on his own account but only on ours. For he could easily do without their labour, since they can do nothing of themselves, but whatever they accomplish is given from heaven. Hence Paul (no less than Peter) says: "Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers through whom you believed, and as the Lord gave to each one? I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase. So neither is he who plants anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase." (1 Cor. 3.5–7)

units.la: 2. Quòd distinguunt Petram seu fundamentum & caput,&c. in Invisibile & Visibile, à veritate alienum est, sensu praesertim Pontificio. Dicunt enim, Christum esse caput Invisibile, quod cùm jam in coelis sit, oculis corporis videri nequeat. Petrum verò caput Visibile, quod in terris, oculis corporeis conspici possit. Atqui
units.tr: 2. The distinction by which they divide the Rock or foundation and the Head into invisible and visible is foreign to the truth, especially in the Papist sense. For they say that Christ is the invisible Head, since he is now in heaven and cannot be seen with bodily eyes, while Peter is the visible Head, who is on earth and can be seen with bodily eyes. But

units.la: 1. Proprie Invisibile dicitur: non quod ob loci distantiam, aut aliud impedimentum, non videtur: ita namque Petrus idem modò visibilis, modò invisibilis dici potuisset: ita Papa: ita quodvis Corpus suâ naturâ visibile: & Christus dū in terris fuit, visibile fuisset caput, nunc in cœlis existens, nobis viatoribus Invisibile, beatis in cœlis Visibile foret: denique rediturus ad judicium toti mundo & post in cœlis erit in æternum, non Invisibile futurum Caput.
units.tr: 1. "Invisible" is properly used not of what is not seen because of distance of place or some other hindrance. For in that sense Peter could be called visible at one time and invisible at another, and so could the Pope, and so could any body that is visible by its nature. And while Christ was on earth he would have been a visible Head, and now, existing in heaven, he is invisible to us who are still on the way, but visible to the blessed in heaven. Finally, when he returns to judgment for the whole world, and afterwards remains in heaven for ever, he will not be an invisible Head.

units.la: Iterum, si ab eo tempore, quo Christus Simoni dixit, Tu es Petrus; Petra & caput constitutus est, tum Christus existens adhuc in terris, Petra & caput quoque fuit, aut non fuit. Si hoc, tum Petrus ante Filium Dei incarnatem [?] caput constitutus ab eo, qui nondum fuit: si vero illud, tum fuerunt simul in terris duo Visibilia capita, &c. nullum Invisibile: quid vero fiet die illo judicii? quid post in cœlis? Aut plane nullum erit tum, aut nullum invisibile caput; Si prius, erit tum Ecclesia ἀκεφάλῳ [?] absque Petra, absque Sponso, &c. Si posterius; evanescet tum distinctio: Sed quid de Petro & de tot illius Successoribus fiet? Aut tum erunt & ipsi capita Ecclesiæ, aut non erunt. Si prius, tum Ecclesia futurum monstrum πολυκέφαλον [?]: Si vero posterius, tum aut erit minor Petri & Successorum dignitas & prærogativa in cœlis, quam ea quam habuerunt in terris; aut, quod verisimilius, tum manifestum fiet, quod nec Petrus, nec quisquam Successorum unquam Petra & Capita fuerint.
units.tr: Again, if from the time when Christ said to Simon, "You are Peter", Peter was constituted Rock and Head, then either Peter was also Rock and Head while Christ was still on earth, or he was not. If the former, then Peter was constituted Head by one who had not yet been made incarnate as the Son of God. If the latter, then there were at the same time two visible heads on earth, and no invisible head. What then will happen on the day of judgment? What afterwards in heaven? Either there will then be no head at all, or no invisible head. If the former, the Church will be [ἀκέφαλος, headless], without Peter, without a Bridegroom, and so on. If the latter, the distinction will vanish. But what will become of Peter and of his many successors? Either they too will then be heads of the Church, or they will not. If the former, the Church will be a [πολυκέφαλον, many-headed] monster. If the latter, then either the dignity and prerogative of Peter and his successors in heaven will be less than what they had on earth, or, what is more likely, it will become plain that neither Peter nor any of his successors was ever a Rock or Head.

units.la: Cæterum, si Christus consideratur in sensu diviso, Qui Petra, caput, &c. est; palam est, quod respectu naturæ divinæ sit invisibilis; respectu vero naturæ humanæ est & manet visibilis in æternum; sicque idem caput visibile & invisibile: ut iterum distinctio in fumum abeat. Si vero Christus consideratur Petra, &c. in sensu composito, id est, Qua est Petra, qua caput, &c. visibilis Petra, visibile caput dici nequit.
units.tr: Furthermore, if Christ is considered in the divided sense, as he who is Rock, Head, and so on, it is clear that in respect of his divine nature he is invisible, but in respect of his human nature he is and remains visible for ever. So the same Head is both visible and invisible, and the distinction again dissolves into smoke. If, on the other hand, Christ is considered as Rock, and so on, in the composite sense, that is, as one who is Rock and Head, then a visible Rock or a visible Head cannot be spoken of.

units.la: Ratio: quia, ut Ecclesia ædificium est spirituale, ita Petra spiritualis: & ut Ecclesia corpus mysticum & spirituale: ita & Christus caput mysticum & spirituale: spirituale autem qua tale, visibile non est. Sicq; denuo in nihilum redigitur Pontificiorum distinctio, & cum distinctione Primatus Petri & Successorum.
units.tr: The reason is this: just as the Church is a spiritual building, so the Rock is spiritual; and just as the Church is a mystical and spiritual body, so Christ is a mystical and spiritual Head. But what is spiritual as such is not visible. So the Papists' distinction, and with it the distinction of the primacy of Peter and his successors, is once again reduced to nothing.

units.la: {*} At, dicunt, Ecclesia in his terris visibilis est; Oportet igitur, ut habeat in his terris visibile caput, visibilem Petram.
units.tr: "But," they say, "the Church is visible on these earth. It is necessary, therefore, that it have a visible Head on earth, a visible Rock."

units.la: esse: At falsum utrumq;: ratio, quia ut Ecclesia semper firma maneat, Petram semper vivam esse oportet, quo argumento Paulus Hebr.7.v.23. in finem usque, probat Christum solum & unicum Sacerdotem N.T. esse.
units.tr: ...is so. But both claims are false. The reason is that, if the Church is to remain always firm, the Rock must be always living. By this argument Paul, in Heb. 7.23 to the end, proves that Christ alone is the one and only priest of the New Testament.

units.la: III. Tertia distinctio, qua dicitur Petra seu Caput aliud in coelis, quod sit Christus : aliud in terris, quod sit Petrus & Successor ipsius; non majoris momenti est, quàm praecedentes; quod tum ex dictis cuivis patet, tum vero ex sequentibus elucescet. quia,
units.tr: III. The third distinction, by which one Rock or Head is said to be in heaven, namely Christ, and another on earth, namely Peter and his successor, is of no greater weight than the preceding ones. This is plain from what has been said, and will become clearer from what follows, because:

units.la: 1. Si Caput in terris idem fit & Caput terrenum; negamus, Ecclesiam tale habere posse caput: quia Christus dicit coram Pilato Joh.18.36. Regnum meum non est ex hoc mundo, &c.
units.tr: 1. If the Head on earth is the same as an earthly Head, we deny that the Church can have such a head, because Christ says before Pilate: "My kingdom is not of this world" (John 18.36).

units.la: 2. Etsi Christus θεάνθρωπος carnem suam in sublime ad dextram Patris sui extulerit; nobis tamen in terris praesentissimus est, non ulla corporis sui invisibili praesentia: sed Deitate sua, Spiritu suo S. merito & efficacia, denique virtute & donis, per verbi ministerium & Sacramentorum administrationem Ecclesiam efficaciter vocando, sanctificando, fidem excitando, eamq; sibi inserendo, justificando, sanctificando, & ad diem illum obsignando, Matth.28.v.19.20.
units.tr: 2. Although Christ, the God-man, has raised his flesh on high to the right hand of his Father, he is nevertheless most present to us on earth. This is not by any invisible presence of his body, but by his Deity, his Holy Spirit, his merit and efficacy, and finally by his power and gifts. Through the ministry of the Word and the administration of the sacraments, he effectively calls the Church, sanctifies it, arouses faith, joins it to himself, justifies and sanctifies it, and seals it for that day (Matt. 28.19, 20).

units.la: 3. Notabilia sunt Christi ad Apostolos verba Matth.23.8,12. ex quibus colligimus: nullum quoque in terris nominari debere Petram, &c. praeter & juxta Christum.
units.tr: 3. Christ's words to the apostles in Matt. 23.8, 12 are noteworthy. From them we gather that no one on earth should be called Rock, and so on, except besides and under Christ.

units.la: 4. Sequeretur, ejusdem Ecclesiae Petram dici posse Petrum, cujus Ecclesiae Petra, Christus est; i.e. non tantum Ecclesiae militantis, sed & triumphantis; non tantum Novi, sed etiam V. Testamenti: quod absurdum.
units.tr: 4. It would follow that Peter could be called Rock of the same Church whose Rock is Christ, that is, not only of the militant Church but also of the triumphant, and not only of the New Testament but also of the Old. This is absurd.

units.la: 5. Vivente Petro, & Christo existente in terra, fuisset in terris biceps Ecclesia: ascendente Christo, & mortuo Petro, prorsus ἀμφίβολος, quod itidem inconveniens. Nec juvat Pontificios successio Episcoporum Romanae Ecclesiae, per quam Hydrae similimam faciunt Ecclesiam.
units.tr: 5. While Peter was living, and Christ was on earth, there would have been a two-headed Church on earth; after Christ ascended and Peter died, the Church would be wholly [ἀμφίβολος, ambiguous], which is likewise unfitting. Nor does the succession of bishops of the Roman Church help the Papists, by which they make the Church very like the Hydra.

units.la: Petrae illi, supra quâ aedificata Ecclesia, nempe Soli Domino nostro Jesu Christo sit laus: Dignus est Agnus ille mactatus, qui accipiat virtutem & divitias, & Sapientiam, & Fortitudinem, & honorem, & gloriam, & benedictionem in secula seculorum. Amen.
units.tr: To that Rock upon which the Church is built, namely to our Lord Jesus Christ alone, be praise: "Worthy is that Lamb that was slain to receive power and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing, for ever and ever. Amen."
